items.title: Cap the Partners list on the home page
items.where: / Partners (index.astro `partners.map` over every listed clinic)
items.problem: Every listed clinic is drawn on the home page with no limit. Today 5 clinics take 892px on a phone (85–111px per card plus a 6px gap). At 30 listed clinics that is about 2,700px more on a phone and at 100 about 9,000px, which also stretches the film's walk and its contrast stops. /find/ already lists, filters and sorts every clinic.
items.proposal: Show up to 6 clinics (the newest listed, or a fixed sample), then 'Find a clinic (N listed)' as the way on. The list is still read live from the directory, so it still names only clinics that are really listed.
items.risk: A clinic not shown may feel left out. Choosing 'newest' rotates fairly. Glass contrast for the shorter card has to be measured again.
items.touches_owner_decision: The Tour: 'Partners — the clinics really listed, read live from the directory'; kept, only capped
items.proposal_final:
Cap the Partners list on the home page only once it outgrows a screen (index.astro, `partners.map`):
- **The cap.** Draw at most 6 clinics (two rows of three on a desk, six cards on a phone). Below that, nothing changes.
- **The selection.** Take the 6 from the same live `loadDirectory()` list in an order that rotates. One option is a shuffle seeded by the Manila date, so it is stable within a day and different the next. Another is a fresh shuffle on each request; the page is already server-rendered. Never use name order or a fixed sample, and no new public field or migration is needed.
- **The way on.** No new link. The head's existing "See every clinic" becomes "See all N clinics" (→ /find/) when the list is capped, so there is still one way to the full list.
- **The empty state.** Its words ("Each one appears here, and on Find a clinic, as it opens") stay; they are only drawn while there are no clinics.
- **Checks.** Re-measure the Partners card's contrast over the film frames behind its new, shorter height (light and dark, 1440 and 390, every 110px of scroll), as "The tour" requires.
- **Note for the owner.** Partner clinics are paying customers, so a one-line note in the plan should say that the home page now shows six at a time, in rotation, and that every listed clinic stays on /find/.

items.title: One frosted-glass recipe instead of seven
items.where: src/pages/websites.astro (258 CSS lines), find/index.astro (273), start/index.astro (225), me/_Door.astro (246), me/_Shell.astro (169), coverage.astro (187), find/_ui/clinic-glass.css (409), global.css .pane-glass
items.problem: Each glass page carries its own fixed room layer, its own token overrides (--c-ink-2, --glass-pane, inner, edge, link, field lines) and both dark twins of them, under its own prefix (wb-, cv-, pt-, cl-, me-, start, pane-). That is about 1,770 lines that do the same thing with slightly different numbers. A change to one token family (a new dark shade, a link colour) means seven edits and seven contrast runs, and a missed dark twin is the bug class CLAUDE.md warns about.
items.proposal: One shared `.glass-page` layer in global.css. It takes the photo (or the clinic's cover) and a darkness level as data attributes, sets one token set with both dark twins once, and pages keep only what is truly theirs. Move one page at a time (/websites/ first, since it is in this area), comparing computed styles before and after, as the Site API section asks.
items.risk: Every line on glass was measured per page over its own photo. Unifying numbers can drop a line below 4.5:1 over one photo (the beige walls, the hedges), so every page must be re-measured light and dark at 1440 and 390. The workspace must not change (compare computed styles).
items.touches_owner_decision: Frosted glass on the public pages (owner, 26 Sep): kept, only its code is shared
items.proposal_final:
One shared frosted-glass layer for the photo-room pages, without unifying numbers that were measured separately.

Scope: /websites/ (wb-), /find/ (pt-), /coverage/ (cv-), /start/, /me/ and /me/code/ (me/_Door), /me/visits/ (me/_Shell), and the clinic page and its booking (cl-). These pages already share the same values: blur 14px saturate 1.4, dark pane rgb(22 27 33 / 0.58), ink-2 #2f3a4a light and #c3cad4 dark, the room dimmed to brightness 0.62 in dark mode, the same @supports fallback for browsers without backdrop-filter, and the same fixed room layer.

Add a `.glass-page` block in global.css, inside `@layer components`, that sets this token set once with both dark-mode copies. Add a small shared component (for example `GlassRoom.astro`) that draws the fixed room from the page's own picture sources and size hints. The photo is passed to the component, not read from a data attribute, because CSS cannot take an image URL from one. Each page keeps only what is truly its own: its prefix's layout classes, me/_Door's deeper link teal (#094f4d / #7fdcd4), /start/'s `--start-ink-2`, and me/_Shell's sidebar overrides, which stay scoped to `.me-shell` so the clinic workspace is untouched.

Kept out on purpose:
(a) The home page's `.pane.pane-glass` over the film. It has its own measured numbers (blur 24px, 60% white, a darker charcoal in dark mode) and its own measuring method (every 110px of scroll and over the poster). At most it reads the shared token names; its values stay as they are.
(b) The staff entrance's `--en-*` card.
(c) What only the clinic page has. It stands on its own uploaded cover or the soft blur, never a house or stock photo, and the shared layer has no default photo. clinic-glass.css keeps the room-tone classes (.cl-room-dark, .cl-room-busy and their wash, veil and 0.7 pane) and the placeholder colour.

No value becomes more transparent or lighter in this change.

Move one page at a time, /websites/ first. After each move, compare computed styles before and after on that page. Then compare them on the workspace, on /c/<slug>/ and on the home page, which must show no difference. Re-measure every line on the glass, light and dark (chosen and device), at 1440 and 390, over that page's own photo and, for the clinic page, over an all-black, an all-white, a striped and an empty cover. The lowest values today are 4.7:1 on the home page and 5.3:1 on the clinic page; nothing may fall below 4.5:1.

Payoff: about six copies of the same token block and its dark-mode copies become one, so a missing dark-mode copy can no longer happen on one page alone.

items.proposal_final:
Retire /clinics/ and send it to Clinic sign-in.

   - CLAUDE.md's Layout line for clinics.astro.

Who it helps: the maintainer has one stale page and its doc and contrast entries fewer, and a staff member with an old bookmark lands where sign-in actually happens. Impact 1, effort S, owner decision: none.

items.proposal: When the booking opens with a held time, show one screen. The strip extends to 'Toothache · Wed 7 Oct, 10:00 am · any dentist [Change]'. Below it: name, mobile, the optional HMO and note, the consent tick, a two-line summary and one teal 'Book 10:00 am'. Change opens the reason, dentist and time choices in place. items.proposal_final:
Book from a tapped time on one screen (workspace clinics only; the request path is unchanged).

When the booking opens with a held time, show one screen.

- **The strip at the top** reads "Toothache · Wed 7 Oct, 10:00 am · any dentist [Change]". At a one-dentist clinic it reads "· with Dr <her name>" (soloDentist), and Change there offers only reason and time.

  - Every dentist row keeps "PRC checked" or "PRC check pending" and their days and hours.
  - The p32 verdict runs again on any change: a longer visit, or a dentist who is not free, turns the strip amber with the sentence and the two nearest free times, or a Call button.
  - The reason's fee-guide price stays on the strip or in the summary.
- **Below the strip:**
  - Who is the visit for: Me / Someone else. Me is ticked, so it costs no tap; Someone else shows the Patient's name field.
  - Name and mobile.

  - One teal "Book 10:00 am", in the normal flow of the card. It is never sticky or fixed to the bottom; if it sits below the fold, shorten what is above it instead.
- **Unchanged:** the 409 path reopens the time choice. Undo (3 minutes) stays. /api/bookings, patient_consent (version, channel 'web', given_by_name, appointment_id) and the in-transaction re-check stay exactly as they are.

items.proposal_final:
Replace the 65-chip time grid with a day row and that day's times (src/pages/find/[clinic]/book.astro, When step: paintSlots, 'Show more days'). Patient-facing.

1. Show one row of day pills for the next 14 days, under the question and on the glass card. Do not put it on the bare room. On a phone the row scrolls sideways inside itself, and the page never scrolls sideways.
   - Each pill is a 44 px radio with its day in words and its count, e.g. "Wed 7 · 12 open".
   - A day with nothing says so in words ("Closed" or "Full"), never with colour alone.
   - Selected: the held time's day if there is one, otherwise the first day with an open time.
   - Under the row, only that day's times, split into Morning and Afternoon, as one radio group.
   - Continue sits directly under the times. Choosing a time never moves the page on by itself: arrow keys in a radio group fire change.

2. Keep the counts honest past the 200-slot cap. Choose one:
   - give the API a per-day count read that is not capped (or a higher cap for this call), or
   - show counts only for days the answer fully covers. Days after the last complete day read "See times" and fetch their own day when chosen. A day past the cap is never shown as 0 or closed.
   Measured on :4620: burnham-smile and marikina-heights already return exactly 200 slots at 30 minutes, with the last day cut short.

3. Keep everything else as it is:
   - p32: the held time pre-selects its day and time. The amber strip keeps its sentence and the two nearest free times. "Continue goes to When" while the held time does not fit.
   - The empty states, including "Nothing open with Dr X in the next two weeks" with the Call button.
   - The closed-days and days-away line, with the solo dentist named by her whole name.
   - The availability data (slotOpen and openSlots) and the 409 path back to When.

4. Measure again: contrast on glass at 4.5:1 or better (light and dark, 1440 and 390, over a busy, black, white and missing cover), 44 px targets, keyboard order, the radio semantics, and Continue's distance from the question at 390.

Impact 4, effort M. Owner decision touched: none.

items.title: Ask 'what's wrong' once and keep the patient's words in the visit
items.where: src/pages/find/[clinic]/book.astro (Reason chips, the payload); src/pages/find/index.astro carry(); find/_ui/ClinicPage.astro Book links; src/pages/api/bookings/index.ts (the insert)
items.problem: The Reason step lists 11 chips, and 'Not sure — a check-up' and 'Just a check-up' are both there, both meaning consultation. 14 more services sit in a fold. The symptom chosen on /find/ is carried by the card's slot and Book links only, not by the name link or 'Clinic page', so the clinic page route asks it again. Then it is thrown away: the walked booking BU-RYFR (patient picked 'Toothache' twice) is saved as reason='Consultation', notes empty. The dentist sees 'Consultation' and the desk has to call to ask what is wrong.
items.proposal: Drop the duplicate check-up chip. Carry ?symptom/?service on every link from a /find/ card, including the clinic page and its Book buttons. Send the chosen label with the booking and store it as the visit's note ('From the booking: Toothache'), which the visit panel already shows read-only for web visits. Leave appointment.reason as the service name, because data.ts reads a service from those words.
items.risk: The note field is the patient's own words (shown read-only, never editable by the desk), so prefix it clearly. Check that the 160-character confirmation text still uses the service name.
items.touches_owner_decision: none
items.proposal_final:
Ask "what's wrong" once and keep the answer with the visit (book.astro, find/index.astro carry(), find/_ui/ClinicPage.astro Book links, api/bookings/index.ts).

1. **Merge the two check-up chips into one.** Use the wording "A check-up, or not sure", with value `consultation`. It is the default when nothing is pre-selected, and `?symptom=checkup` selects it too. Keep the help line's reassurance that not being sure is a fine answer.
2. **Carry the choice on every link from a /find/ card.** The clinic name, Clinic page and the card's slot and Book links all carry `?symptom` or `?service`. The clinic page passes it on to its own Book buttons. Urgent symptoms are still never pre-selected on the booking page; it already filters them through `bookable`.
3. **Send the symptom's id with the booking** (a new `symptom` field next to `service`). The server looks the id up in `symptoms` and ignores anything it does not know. It stores the label as the first line of `appointment.notes` (for example "Picked: Toothache"), then whatever the patient typed. All of it stays inside the existing 500-character limit. Do not start it with "From the booking". The visit panel already shows the note under "Visit note", and Edit shows it under "From the booking", read-only for web and request visits.
4. **Leave `appointment.reason` as the service name**, because data.ts reads the service from it. The confirmation and reminder texts keep using `service.name`.

No migration and no change to the privacy notice: "what for" is already in "What we keep".

items.proposal_final:
Put the urgent help first on a phone. Change `src/pages/find/index.astro`, the symptom order in `src/data/directory.ts` and `patient.css`.

(a) Show the urgent chips at the start of the row on a phone, so they are in the first screen. Two ways:
- reorder the list to Toothache, Swelling or fever, Knocked-out tooth, then the rest (Toothache is the most common reason, so it keeps first place), or
- add one line in the soft-red alert style above the row: "Swelling, fever or a knocked-out tooth? Call now", which selects the urgent chip.
The booking's Reason chips are not affected, because they filter out the urgent symptoms.

(b) When an urgent symptom is chosen:
- Sort clinics that are open now to the top, and mark them with the existing status pill (words, not colour alone).
- Do not switch on the Open now filter. If it were on, a night or Sunday visit would hide every clinic and its phone number.
- Move each card's Call button to the front of its actions, ahead of Book, but keep it quiet. At most, make only the first open clinic's Call the screen's one teal button. Never a solid Call on every card: the rule is one teal button per screen.
- Keep the alert callout's emergency-room sentence word for word.
- If no clinic is open, add one line saying so ("No clinic is open right now. Call the one that opens soonest, or go to the nearest emergency room if…"), above the list, not in place of it.

(c) On a phone, cut the intro card to the h1. Drop the eyebrow and the lede under 640 px, or fold the lede's "No account" into the h1 card. The first card's times then sit in the first screen (about 120 px saved).

Re-measure contrast on the glass in light and dark at 390 and 1440, and check that targets are at least 44 px.

items.title: Show the next open times on the clinic page

items.problem: The /find/ card shows the next 3 open times, but the clinic page (both /find/<slug>/ and the clinic's own /<slug>/) shows none: 0 open-time links were measured. A patient who opens the clinic page to learn more, or arrives from a dentist page, Google or the clinic's own site, must enter the booking and pass Reason and Dentist to see any time. That route took 10 taps to reach Confirm and went through the 65-chip When grid.
items.proposal: Under 'Book a slot' on a live clinic, show 'Next open: Today 12:30 pm · 1 pm · Tomorrow 9 am' as held-time links (book/?slot=…), as the /find/ card already does. That way most bookings use the short held-time path.
items.risk: One more availability read per clinic page view (as /find/ already does for every card). The glass contrast of the slot chips needs measuring over the clinic's own cover photo.
items.touches_owner_decision: none
items.proposal_final:
Show the next open times on a live clinic's page. This is the same pattern as the /find/ card, so a patient learns one way to see and pick times.

Where:
- src/pages/find/_ui/ClinicPage.astro, in the head glass card right under the action row (Book a slot · Call · Directions). That covers both /find/<slug>/ and the clinic's own /<slug>/.
- In the frontmatter, call `openSlots(l, { limit: 3 })` only when `l.workspace` is true, as /find/index.astro does.

What it shows:
- The label "Next open", then 3 quiet `.slot` links ("Today 2 pm · 2:30 pm · 3 pm") to `/find/<slug>/book/?slot=<slotIso>`. This is the existing held-time path: the booking opens with the time on its strip and skips When while it fits.
- A live clinic with nothing open in 14 days shows /find/'s own sentence: "Nothing open in the next two weeks — call the clinic."
- A request-only clinic shows nothing new; its request callout already explains.

What does not change:
- "Book a slot" stays the page's one teal button. The chips stay inside the glass card, never on the bare room.
- No new words or classes beyond a small flex-row rule in clinic-glass.css.

Measure before shipping:
- Contrast of the label and the chips, light and dark, at 1440 and 390, over a real cover, all-black, all-white, harsh stripes and no photo. The page's existing standard is 0 fails, lowest 5.3:1.
- 44 px targets and no sideways scroll at 390.

Expected result:
- A patient on the clinic page who can come at one of the next 3 times reaches Confirm in 7 taps over 4 screens instead of 9 over 5. They skip the 62-chip, 1328-px-tall When screen.
- They also see at a glance whether there is anything today or tomorrow before starting.
- The cost is about 55–60 px of page height and 3 extra controls in the first screen.
- It also makes true the "Open slots" that /find/<slug>/'s meta description already promises.

Out of scope, for the /dentists/ audit: a dentist page's "Book here" skips the clinic page and does not preselect that dentist.

items.proposal_final:
Title: List a new clinic in one save.

Where: settings/_ui/ProfileSection.astro (the listing block, the About field, the "Ready to be found" checklist), plus the heldText wording in settings/_lib/profile.ts. No page script.

1. **Enable the switch from the server.** Render input[name=listed] disabled only when something this form cannot supply is missing (opening hours, or a dentist with days here). It shows on Find a clinic as soon as both are in."
   - saveClinic already lists in that same post, because okToList reads p.about.
   - If the About is still empty, the existing held path saves everything else and says "Saved. The clinic is not listed: it still needs a few sentences about the clinic." Keep that sentence.
   - This also works with scripts off.

2. **Put the About under the switch while it is empty.** While the clinic is not listed and its About is empty, draw the one About textarea inside the listing block, directly under the switch, with its counter. Once an About is saved, it is drawn in "Your clinic" as now.
   - Render exactly one name="about" field. Two would post two values, and form.get takes the first.
   - With About up there, the pane head's Save is on the first screen at 1440. At 390 it is within about 300 px.

3. **One message, not three.**
   - Drop "Then switch this on and save" from the switch's line.
   - Split the checklist into what listing needs (counted: About, hours, a dentist) and "Also worth doing" (HMOs, a photo; not counted). Then a clinic one step from listable no longer reads "2 of 5 done".
   - Keep the welcome note's first sentence only.

Result for a clinic made at /start/:
- Before: Go, type, scroll ~1000 px up to Save, Save, page load, tick, Save. That is 5 actions, 2 saves and 2 page loads.
- After: type, tick, Save. That is 3 actions, 1 save and 1 page load.

Nothing legally or clinically needed is touched, and no owner decision is involved.

Check: profile-check.mjs, plus a sign-up run at 1440 and 390 that lists the clinic in one save, holds when the About is left empty, and holds when hours are removed. Measure contrast on the moved block in light and dark.

**Title:** The first screen after sign-up is a short "get ready" view. Clinic profile becomes only the clinic's public details. No saved value can be lost by the split.

**Where:**
- /start/ → /c/<slug>/settings/?welcome=1
- settings/_ui/ProfileSection.astro
- settings/_lib/profile.ts (saveClinic, savedProfile, missingForListing)
- settings/_lib/common.ts (SECTIONS)
- settings/index.astro (`may`, SECTION_OF, the hash script)

**The welcome view.** ?welcome=1, and Clinic profile while the clinic is unlisted, open on the existing "Ready to be found" checklist:
- the About box and the listing switch, as a small form of their own (form=listing);
- one Go link for each item still missing;
- one teal Save.

The checklist and the switch both read missingForListing(), so they never disagree: the switch stays disabled until the About box, opening hours and a dentist are in. Optionally, one more line: "Name your data protection officer" → #privacy (RA 10173). It is shown, never required to list. On a phone the view sits above the section list.

**A new section, "How you work".** It holds chairs, walk-ins, PhilHealth accreditation, booking mode, the two text switches, and 044's turnover, held reminders and consent question. It moves:
- the TIN and BIR branch code under its More, keeping the sentence "Printed on statements from Finances. Flossify does not issue BIR receipts…" word for word;
- its own Save, under settings.edit, with every 044 default and every word unchanged ("It never stops the visit").

Clinic profile keeps the name, city, address, phone, email, Maps link, About, the founding year, HMOs and the clinic's own page and sign-in address. It has one Save (the bottom twin goes).

**Integrity rule (required).**
- Every split form carries a presence flag for each group of fields it holds: has_listing, has_public, has_work (or has_work_choices), has_tax.
- saveClinic changes only the groups a post carries and keeps every other column as saved. That covers listed, philhealth_dental, booking_mode, walk_ins, remind_48h, recall_texts, chairs and the HMO ticks.
- An old tab's single form (which carries everything) still saves as today.
- This protects the 017 accreditation trigger: the PhilHealth payor must never be switched off by a form that did not show the PhilHealth choice.
- Check: post each form alone and compare the clinic row and hmo_provider before and after. Only the posted group may change.

**Optional folds (10 → 7):** Closed days into Opening hours, Photos into Clinic profile, Roles into People.
- Each folded part keeps its own permission gate: the Roles part is drawn only with roles.manage, and SECTION_OF 'role' still checks roles.manage on post.
- Each folded panel keeps one teal button: the second action goes quiet (Add closed days, Add photos, Add role).
- Privacy is not folded or hidden.
- Old ids and anchors (#closed, #photos, #roles, #work, #hmos, #tax, #about, #listing) keep landing through the hash script. A refused post still opens its own part.

**Tell the owner** (no question needed): How the day runs is now under Clinic settings → How you work. Update HANDOFF.md, CLAUDE.md ("How the day runs (044)") and the review notes that say "Clinic profile → How the day runs".

**Update the checks:** choices-check.mjs and profile-check.mjs for the new places, plus the per-form integrity check above.

2. Unlock adds only what is its own after success: the device.unlock audit, endHandover, clearPark, then its redirect.
3. Put `helloFor(date)` and `demoLoginsOn()` beside it, and use them from login.astro and the door. login.astro's email POST (authenticate, login:e:, the branch choice) stays as it is.
4. Pass each page's miss sentence and its links (the door's Forgot link, unlock's lack of one) in from the page, so this refactor changes no words. Whether unlock should also say "Check the password, or ask your clinic owner to reset it" and show Forgot is a separate wording question. items.risk: Usernames are unique only within a group, so a username without a clinic must never be guessed across clinics; the clinic field is required for that path. Error words must not reveal whether a clinic address exists beyond what the door already shows.
items.touches_owner_decision: none (the clinic doors and usernames are the owner's 029 design; this only shortens the way to them)
items.proposal_final:
On /auth/login/ (the email door, reached when the device remembers no clinic), relabel the first field "Email or username". If what is typed has no "@", the card asks on the same card for "Your clinic's address (flossify.ph/…)". With scripts on, the field is revealed by toggling the `hidden` attribute. With scripts off, a post with no "@" and no address comes back with the field shown and one sentence. The username and password are never sent anywhere until the address is there.

The post resolves the address with clinicDoor(), the same parsing as findClinics. This also covers a clinic whose slug is on RESERVED and has no /<slug>/ page. It then runs the door's own sign-in, moved out of [clinic]/sign-in.astro into one shared function used by both pages:
- the same CSRF check
- the same counts `login:u:<slug>:<login>` and `login:ip:<ip>`, with the refund on success
- authenticateAt (staff_access to that clinic only, never a guess across clinics)
- the same auth_event rows: login.ok, login.fail and login.locked, as `<login>@<slug>`
- must_change_password as today
- rememberClinic on success, so the bar's Clinic sign-in opens that clinic's door from then on

The error words are the door's own. An address that is no clinic gets one sentence that says no more than the door's 404 already does.

To keep the measured entrance rule (button above the fold at 1366×768; no scrolling at all at 1440×900, where the page is exactly 900 px tall today), the extra field must not add height overall. Do that by folding "Sign in at your clinic's page" into a quieter line or the fallback. /auth/clinic/ stays as the fallback, and it still searches listed clinics only by name. Keep 50 px fields at 16 px, 44 px targets, and measure contrast again in light and dark at 1440 and 390.

On Add member's "password" success line, add a quiet "Copy sign-in details" button. It copies the door address and the username only, never the password, including a "make one for me" password.

Expected result: about 6 actions on 3 screens become 4 actions on 1 screen for a username-only member on a new device.

items.title: The sign-up owner is assumed to treat patients: ask the same 'treats patients' question as Add member
items.where: /start/ (start/index.astro), signup_clinic() (006: staff slug, practices {General dentistry}, staff_schedule Mon–Sat), public_directory(), /admin/prc/
items.problem: signup_clinic() gives every new owner a public slug, 'General dentistry' and the clinic's six days. So the owner is listed on the clinic's public page as a dentist, satisfies the listing's 'a dentist with days at this branch', and is queued on /admin/prc/, whether or not they treat. A business owner or manager who is not a dentist would be published as one. Add member already asks this with one switch ('treats patients', RoleField.astro); sign-up does not.
items.proposal: Add one Yes/No to /start/ 'You' section: 'Do you treat patients at this clinic?'. Default Yes, the main persona. With No, signup_clinic leaves out the slug and schedule; the setupState checklist then shows 'Add a dentist' and the PRC queue gets nobody. This needs a new migration replacing signup_clinic (never edit 006).
items.risk: It adds one control to sign-up. With No, the clinic cannot be listed until a dentist is added; the checklist must say so plainly.
items.touches_owner_decision: PRC checks and public dentist claims (keeps both truthful); none reversed
items.proposal_final:
On /start/, in the "You" card, add one question asked the way Add member asks it: "Do you treat patients at this clinic?" Yes or No, default Yes. Show the existing PRC field only under Yes, as Add member's dentist-only fields do (data-team-dentist), and keep it optional as it is today. With No, write a new migration that replaces signup_clinic(); never edit 006. The new function leaves out owner_slug, practices, prc_licence and the staff_schedule rows. staff.role stays 'owner', so nothing changes about permissions.

Also change the "What happens next" card for the No answer: "Patients can't find or book the clinic until a dentist is added: Clinic settings → People → Add member." The listing checklist line "a dentist with days at this branch" should link to Add member.

The new part is a way back, needed in both directions. An owner's row should be able to switch "Treats patients" for themselves, on their own person page or on My page.
- Turning it on gives them a slug, General dentistry and the clinic's days. It asks for the PRC number and puts them in the /admin/prc/ queue as pending.
- Turning it off removes the slug and the schedule column after one confirming question. It keeps the PRC and PTR rules people.ts already applies to someone who stops treating.

Today an owner's "treats" is locked (roleLocked), and an owner without a slug can never get one. Without this change, a wrong answer at sign-up could not be undone. It also lets owners already published as dentists who do not treat take themselves off. Audit the change as staff.edit, the same as any other change of professional side. The impact stays at 2; the effort is M for sign-up alone and M to L with the way back.

items.proposal_final:
Title: "A shorter code page, and one sign-in link on /start/"

Where: /auth/code/ (src/pages/auth/code.astro) and /start/ (src/pages/start/index.astro). Who: desk, dentist, owner resetting or accepting an invitation; a new clinic owner.

**1. /auth/code/: one password field.**
- Ask for the new password once: "New password", the Show button and the length rule under it.
- Remove "Type it again" and the "The two passwords don't match" branch. Keep passwordProblem() as the only rule.
- Why this is safe: the person has just received a code on this channel, so a typo costs one more code from "Didn't get a text?".

**2. /auth/code/: when the number is already known, merge the note and the field into one line.**
- This applies only when the mobile or email came from the fl_code_phone / fl_code_email cookie.
- The note "If that number belongs…" and the Mobile field become one line: "If 0917 000 0000 is on a staff account, a code is on its way. It works for 15 minutes." plus a link "Another number?" to /auth/forgot/. A code for another number needs a new request anyway.
- The value travels in a hidden input.
- Never "Code sent to …": the cookie is set whether or not the number is on file, and the page must not say otherwise.
- With no cookie (an invitation typed on another device), the field stays as it is. "Came by email?" keeps working.
- Expected result at 390: from 1388 px with the submit at 1168 down to about 1250 px with the submit at about 1030. It still scrolls on a phone, so do not claim the button comes into view.
- At 1440: the form stays within 1366×768.

**3. /start/: one sign-in link and one listing sentence.**
- Keep the lede's "Already set up? Sign in" and remove the aside's duplicate. The bar already has Clinic sign-in.
- Say the listing rule once, in the go-note beside the button, and trim the aside's third tick to what is not said elsewhere ("the desk gives each request a time; switch to live booking in Clinic settings").

**4. Keep the confirm field on /start/ and on My page (account).**
- These set the password of the only person nobody can reset: an owner is managed only by an owner, /admin/ has no reset, email is off, and text reset has not had its first live send.
- Do give /start/'s password field the Show button it lacks, using the same data-show pattern as sign-in. Measure its contrast on the glass card, light and dark, at 1440 and 390, as CLAUDE.md requires.
- Revisit dropping the confirm field on these two pages once launch.md's Semaphore test has passed. If it is dropped then, re-record register-clinic.mp4 with scripts/record-walkthroughs.mjs and update scripts/dev/glass/signup-e2e.mjs.

Leave Add member and Set a new password as they are: those are temporary passwords their owner will change.

Impact 1–2. Effort S: no migration, and neither the walkthrough video nor signup-e2e is affected. Check by re-measuring /auth/code/ at 390 and 1440 (cookie and no-cookie), the start/code entrance checks, keyboard order, and the 44 px targets.

items.title: A way back on a handed-over desk device while the patient is still filling in
items.where: /f/i/<token>/ (f/i/[token].astro: 'For the clinic' only on closed and thank-you pages), /auth/unlock/
items.problem: Handing this device to a patient takes 6 desk actions, and taking it back takes 2 (username pre-filled). Both are fine. But while the forms are open, the device shows no way back: 'For the clinic' renders only on a closed or finished page (measured: not visible on page 1). If the patient hands the device back halfway, or the desk needs it urgently, the only route is typing /auth/unlock/ into the address bar.
items.proposal: Add a small quiet 'For the clinic' link to the page foot on every page of a handed-over desk device (deviceKind === 'desk'), not only closed ones. It leads to a full sign-in (unlock), so it opens nothing for the patient, and their typed answers stay saved for when the desk hands the device back.
items.risk: A patient may tap it by mistake. They see a staff sign-in that opens nothing, and Back returns them to their form. Keep it quiet and away from Continue.
items.touches_owner_decision: none
items.proposal_final:
On a desk device handed to a patient (deviceKind === 'desk'), show one quiet "For the clinic" button (btn-quiet, user icon, at least 44 px, never teal) on every open screen of /f/i/<token>/, not only on closed and thank-you pages. It leads to /auth/unlock/.

- **Where it goes:** in the frosted head bar (.ip-bar, the clinic badge row), on the glass. That is where "Ask the desk" already sits, and it keeps the button far from Continue. It must not go in a page foot, a footer or anywhere on the bare cover photo.
- **What it opens:** the full staff sign-in, so nothing opens for the patient. After a sign-in the existing rules apply: device.unlock and intake.stop are audited, the link retires as stopped, and the desk lands on Check with "Stopped. What they saved is kept; send the forms again when ready."
- **What is lost:** state it plainly in the plan. Screens the patient already posted are kept. What is typed on the open screen is lost, both on a mistaken tap (Back reloads the page from the server) and when the desk unlocks. If that is not acceptable, the button can post the current screen first, the way "Ask the desk" does, before going to /auth/unlock/ (effort S→M).
- **Measuring:** contrast ≥ 4.5:1 on the glass, light and dark, at 1440 and 390, over a real room, an all-black, an all-white and a harshly striped cover. Also check 44 px targets and keyboard order (it should come after the form's own controls, or be clearly separate).
- **Testing:** add it to phone-e2e.mjs's desk-device path, with two checks: the button is present on page 1 and on a consent form, and it is absent on a phone and on a clinic tablet.

items.proposal_final:
Title: One name for each staff action in the clinic workspace.

Where:
- src/components/ws/cal/panels.ts (line 261 'Charge this visit', 275 'Book a visit', 353 'Charge this visit' / 'Charge')
- src/pages/c/[clinic]/calls/index.astro:463 ('Book again')
- src/pages/c/[clinic]/finances/close/index.astro:389 ('Rebook')
- src/pages/c/[clinic]/patients/[patient].astro:1213 (text 'Book a visit')
- src/pages/c/[clinic]/patients/_record/VisitStrip.astro:152 ('Charge this visit')
- src/pages/c/[clinic]/finances/index.astro:408 ('Charge this patient')
- src/layouts/Clinic.astro and the record's More menu ('New charge')

Who: desk, dentist, owner.

Proposal: inside /c/<slug>/ only, use one label per action.

Booking is "New booking" everywhere it opens the booking panel. In a list of patients (Calls, Close the day), each link carries an sr-only ": <patient name>". Calls already does this; Close the day's link needs it added.

Charging is "New charge" from a menu or a blank start, and "Charge" from a visit or a patient. Keep every link exactly as it is today. In particular the visit's link must still open finances/new/?visit=<id> with the treatments filled in, so a treatment is never charged twice.

Record the labels in docs/workspace-redesign.md's Shell API under a heading marked "workspace (staff) only". Patient pages keep their own words: /find/, a clinic's own site and /me/ keep "Book a visit", and a clinic not on the workspace keeps "Request a visit". Never relabel a request as a booking, and never relabel "Place" on an unplaced web request.

Update the check scripts that find buttons by text (dash-check, choices-check, seat-check, phone-e2e, paper-check) in the same change.

Impact: 2. Effort: S. Risk: wording only, inside the workspace. Owner decision touched: none.

items.title: A dentist with nothing today sees the clinic, with one line about themselves
items.where: /c/<slug>/ Dashboard; index.astro (filterOf / byDefault for isDentist), board.ts emptyText, patients.ts empty state
items.problem: Hazel (not in on Tuesdays) opened on her own empty, hatched column. She saw two empty messages ('Nothing booked for you on this day' + New booking + 'Dr. Tabanao not in · all day', and 'Nobody has a visit with you today') while the tiles said 3 booked, 1 waiting, 1 in the chair. To see the clinic's day she must press Everyone each time.
items.proposal: When a dentist has no visit today, open on Everyone with one line: 'You are not in today. Next in: Wed 7 Oct.' Mine stays one tap away. Show a single empty state, not two.
items.risk: Small; the opening view changes for a dentist on a day off.
items.touches_owner_decision: Question for the owner: 3 Oct says 'A dentist's Dashboard still opens on their own column'. Ask whether that should give way on the dentist's days off.
items.proposal_final:
**Two parts.**

**(a) Do now, no owner decision needed: one empty state, not two.**
- When the Mine view of today has no visits, the calendar's empty line (board.ts `emptyText`) and Today's patients' empty line (patients.ts line 281) say it once.
- That line names the dentist's next day in from `staff_schedule` and `clinic_block`, for example "Dr. Tabanao is not in today · next in Wed 7 Oct", and offers Everyone as a quiet link.
- Use "not in today" only when `clinic_unavailable()` gives an `hours` or `leave` range for that dentist covering the day. Otherwise say "Nothing booked with you today".

**(b) Only if the owner says yes: a dentist with no visit today opens on Everyone.**
- This is the `filterOf` / `byDefault` default in index.astro, for isDentist.
- It applies only when the page is today and no `?dentist=` was asked for.
- The same one line about the dentist sits above the calendar. Mine stays one tap away in the Mine · Everyone control.
- A visit booked for the dentist during the day does not switch the view while the page is open (the 30-second refresh never changes the filter). The next load of the page opens on Mine as before.
- Every other day, and any day with a visit for the dentist, opens on the dentist's own column exactly as today. That is the 3 Oct rule.
- No permission changes: dentists can already open `?dentist=all`.
- Measure afterwards: one empty state at 1440 and 390, contrast of 4.5:1 or better light and dark, 44 px targets, and dash-check.mjs updated for the day-off case.
items.owner_question: On a day when a dentist has no patients booked with them, should their Dashboard open on the whole clinic's day instead of their own empty column? "Mine" would stay one tap away.

items.proposal_final:
One form for blocked time. Make the Dashboard's Block panel (src/components/ws/cal/BlockPanel.astro → /api/schedule/blocks → addBlock) the only place a dated block is added.

- In Settings → Closed days (settings/_ui/ClosedSection.astro), keep the list of every block ahead, with who added it and when, and keep its quiet Remove as the plain form that works with scripts off (form=closed-remove, settings.edit, removeBlock, audit schedule.unblock).
- Replace the section's add form and its teal "Add closed days" with a link to /c/<slug>/?new=block. A whole-day closure or leave is the panel's "All day" tick, which is checked by default.
- Show that link only to people with schedule.edit. Anyone else sees one line: "Ask someone who can change the schedule to add closed days." Do not quietly widen the API's gate.
- Delete the closed-add branch of closedDaysAction and readWholeDays only once nothing posts to them.
- Take Block time out of the shell's + New menu (Clinic.astro). Keep calendar More → Block time and the ?new=block route that Settings now uses.
- Nothing else changes: addBlock, the book's lock, the schedule.block / schedule.unblock audit, reopenNewlyClosed, the inside-visits list and its link to Calls → In closed time, the held-reminder behaviour (044), the Blocked strip, and clinic_unavailable() for online booking.
- Re-check the 7-role snapshot (snap.mjs/cmp.mjs) after the change. The Settings section and the New menu change for Owner and Admin and should change for no other role.

items.proposal_final:
Title: Remove the dead branches the Dashboard still carries, starting with the old status POST, which skips the role and consent checks.

Where: `src/pages/c/[clinic]/index.astro`, `src/components/ws/routes.ts`, `src/layouts/Clinic.astro`, `src/components/ws/cal/board.ts` (`calUrl`) and `cal/patients.ts` (`state`), and the pages that pass `finance=`.

Who: maintainer. Clinic owners benefit too: their role and consent settings then hold on every path.

Problem:
- **The POST handler.** `index.astro` lines 75–91 still accept a form post that changes a visit's status. Nothing in the app posts there any more. But the handler calls `applyStatus()` directly, so it skips everything `PATCH /api/schedule` enforces:
  - the `schedule.edit` permission (a custom role without it can still change statuses this way);
  - the consent question at In the chair, or at Arrived / In the lobby where the clinic asks at the door, so no `consent_override` is recorded when a patient is seated past an unsigned form;
  - the schedule API's gate and rate limit.
- **The `LANDED` flags.** All are true, so every fallback in `routes.ts` is dead (`/schedule/`, `/billing/`, `#patients`, `#web-title`).
- **New charge.** The New menu's New charge goes through the `/billing/new/` redirect.
- **The `finance` prop.** It is unused (Clinic.astro says so), and the `Section` values `today` / `schedule` / `billing` are never passed.
- **`pf` / `pq`.** They are always `'all'` / `''`, but `board.ts` still writes them into the address.

Proposal:
1. Delete the Dashboard's POST handler now, without waiting on access logs: no page posts to it, and it bypasses checks that the API enforces. Also delete:
   - the `?stale=1` / `?refused=1` callout that only that handler reaches, and the imports it leaves unused;
   - the `pf` / `pq` writer in `calUrl` and the constant `boot.pf` / `boot.pq`.

   A POST to `/c/<slug>/` then gets the default answer (405). Status changes stay one path: `PATCH /api/schedule`, with its permission, consent and lock rules unchanged.
2. Delete the `LANDED` flags and their fallbacks, and point `newCharge` at `/c/<slug>/finances/new/`.
3. Drop the `finance` prop from Clinic.astro and from the pages that pass it, in one change. Drop the dead `Section` values.
4. Keep `/today/` (the installed app's `start_url` and shortcut), `/schedule/` and the `/billing/…` redirects (pages left open before the move) as they are. Keep the `?pq` / `?pf` read-side redirect one more release, then remove it.

Check:
- grep that nothing posts to `/c/<slug>/`.
- Re-run `seat-check.mjs` and `dash-check.mjs`.
- Run the 030 role snapshot (`snap.mjs` / `cmp.mjs`) to show the tabs, buttons and links are identical before and after.

Impact: 1 (maintainer), plus closing a gap in the consent and role rules. Effort: S.

Risk:
- No real client posts to the Dashboard. A hand-made post gets a 405 instead of a status change, which is the point.
- Dropping the `finance` prop touches about a dozen page headers, mechanically.

Touches owner decision: none. It enforces the existing ones ("Going ahead without a consent form asks why … and never blocks"; roles read with `can()`, "each page and API refuses on its own").

items.title: One rule and one engine for the consent to treatment
items.where: _record/VisitStrip.astro (consent line: reads loadVisitConsents only), [patient].astro:491, /patients/<id>/sign/<visit>/ (035), consent-docs.ts + intake (039), /f/[key] (028), visit_treatment_consented() in 039
items.problem: The same words (treatment-2026-09, TREATMENT_CONSENT) are recorded by three engines behind three gates. The tablet signing (visit_consent, 035) is offered whenever the words exist, with no review gate. The intake's general consent (consent_document, 039: phone, tablet, handed device, paper) waits for CONSENT_REVIEWED. The poster forms (patient_consent channel 'form', 028) wait for FORMS_PRIVACY_VERSIONS. So production offers these unreviewed words through 035 only. visit_treatment_consented() counts 035 and 039, but the This visit strip's 'Consent to treatment: not signed · Sign on this tablet' checks only 035. A general consent signed for the visit through the intake would therefore show 'signed' and 'not signed' at once (read from code, not reproduced). The test patient who signed the general consent on her phone today will still be asked to sign on the tablet at her next visit. The record shows three different buttons: strip 'Sign on this tablet', visit panel 'Sign consent on this tablet', page 2 'Prepare forms'.
items.proposal: First, use visit_treatment_consented() everywhere a visit's consent is shown (strip, visit panel, Dashboard), as a small fix now. Then ask the owner and the lawyer one question: is the treatment consent signed once per record (again when the words change) or once per visit? Make the answer one engine (039 consent_document), with the tablet as one channel; /sign/<visit>/ becomes that flow for one form, and 035 rows stay readable as history. Put all copies of the same words behind one review gate.
items.risk: Legal. Existing visit_consent signatures and seals must keep showing exactly as signed. Changing the gate may switch off the only treatment consent path in production until review, so sequence it with the lawyer's sign-off.
items.touches_owner_decision: Touches the owner's 035 request (the patient signs on an iPad per visit), CONSENT_REVIEWED and the lawyer's review. Put this to the owner as a question.
items.proposal_final:
One rule for the consent to treatment. Step 1 now; the rest only after the owner answers.

1. **Now: one answer to "consent to treatment signed for this visit".** No owner decision is involved.
   - Use `visit_treatment_consented()`'s rule (a 035 tablet signing, or an agreed 039 form of kind treatment for that visit) in the This visit strip. That is `[patient].astro:491` plus the `consent` line in `_record/VisitStrip.astro`.
   - Use the same rule for the visit panel's empty line and its button (`_record/VisitPanels.astro:42–77`).
   - Count the agreed general consent form once. Drop the duplicate "signed" pill when the strip's consent line already says it.
   - Give the strip and the panel one label: "Sign on this tablet".
   - Do not change the Dashboard (`cal/data.ts` already uses the rule) or `seatingGaps`.
   - Leave the `/sign/<visit>/` page and the 035 rows exactly as they are.
   - Check: one visit with only a tablet signing, one with only an intake general consent for the visit, and one with neither. The strip, the panel and the Dashboard must agree each time.

2. **Ask the owner, with the lawyer: per visit (today's 035 rule) or once per record.** Only after that answer, consider making `/sign/<visit>/` the tablet channel of the 039 `consent_document` engine for one form. Conditions:
   - The patient still signs with a finger on the clinic's tablet at the visit.
   - The desk's flow is no longer than today's: strip → step 1 → hand the tablet over → sign → thank you. Count it before and after.
   - Existing `visit_consent` rows, signatures and audit lines stay stored and drawn exactly as signed. Nothing is migrated or rewritten.
   - If the answer is "per visit", leave both engines as they are and stop after step 1.

3. **The review gate is not part of this simplification.**

items.proposal_final:
**Title:** Give the chart back the first screen at the chair: a compact This visit strip

**Where:** _record/VisitStrip.astro; components/ws/cal/panels.ts (fillCheck); a new pure rules module shared by both (no Node imports, like block-words.ts). The record head (.pp-top) is not changed.

**Who:** dentist, desk

**Problem:** For a patient in the chair, the head (207 px, 17 controls) and the This visit strip (393 px, 6 lines, 10 controls) push the chart to 922 px, below the 900 px first screen at 1440. The same before/after checklist is written twice:
- on the Dashboard's visit panel (fillCheck, in the browser)
- on the record's strip (on the server)

The two disagree on tone. The Dashboard makes BP not taken and health over 12 months amber; the strip makes BP not taken plain.

**Proposal:**

1. **Safety lines stay as amber or red lines, never folded.** Each keeps its one action.
   - Health history not asked, or last checked over a year ago (Ask now / No change / Something changed).
   - Blood pressure out of range, always: alert at 180/110 or 160/100, warn otherwise (Take again / What to do).
   - Blood pressure not taken, while the visit has not finished (Take it). Do not make this depend on anaesthesia: nothing records that. If a dentist wants it narrowed, that goes in the review pack first.
   - Consent to treatment not signed, with "(a parent or guardian signs)" for a minor (Sign on this tablet).
   - Each consent form not agreed (Open the form / Go ahead anyway, with its reason panel).
   - Privacy notice missing (Record it).
   - Medical clearance waiting for the physician (See the letter). This is new on the strip, taken from fillCheck.
2. **Everything else that is still to do folds into one line of links.** "Still to do: clinical note · treatment · next check-up · charge". Each link opens the same panel or anchor as today.
3. **Done items become one row of pills.** Any "went ahead anyway" stays as its own pill.
4. **"Also:" (Prescription · X-ray or photo · Chart) joins that same row.** It does not get a row of its own.
5. **One set of rules for both screens.** The shared module decides which items exist, their tone and their order. Where the two current versions differ, it takes the stricter tone. Each screen still draws in its own way.
6. **Keep the visit stamp where it is.** Keep the hidden `visit` on the strip's health-checked form and its consent-override panel. The other panels already carry visitId from [patient].astro.
7. **Leave the head alone.** Its safety chips (allergies, conditions, medicines, under 18, BP, clearance, stale health) are untouched.

**Then measure:**
- The chart starts inside 900 px at 1440 for a patient in the chair who has no safety lines.
- With every safety line present, the lines all still show unfolded, at ≥ 4.5:1 contrast in light and dark, 44 px targets, at 390 px.
- paper-check, dash-check and seat-check still pass.

**Impact:** 4 · **Effort:** M

**Risk:** Folding a safety prompt is the one thing to avoid; the list in step 1 is the floor. A shared module that took the weaker of the two tones would quietly demote the Dashboard's amber lines.

**Touches owner decision:** It fits the owner's record requests ("simple, uneventful but effective"; "less space consuming and more organized"; "simpler and less spacious") and 036's "words plus its one action, never a blocked step". It keeps the content and changes only its weight.

1. **More menu.** Cut More to what has no other home: New charge (finance.bill) and Bring in past visits. Clinical note, Add to plan, Prescription, Take blood pressure, Dental certificate and Add X-ray or photo go; each keeps its plus where it lives:

items.title: One patient writer and one chart-number rule; drop dead parts
items.where: type.astro and import.ts (nextChartNos), patient-add.ts, api/schedule/index.ts (nextChartNo SQL), api/bookings/index.ts ('W-' count+1), schema.sql (form_template, form_response), panels.ts fillCheck vs VisitStrip, four page-local Refused copies
items.problem: Four code paths insert patients, with three numbering behaviours: P- from nextChartNos, P- from a separate SQL function, and W- from count+1, which CLAUDE.md already notes fails after a manual delete. Today's intake gave P-0001 beside the clinic's SR-0142..0144. form_template and form_response have 0 rows and no code reference. The visit checklist and the Refused class are each written more than once.
items.proposal: Create one newPatient(tx, …) with one chart-number rule: the clinic's own prefix continuing its sequence. Drop the unused tables in a new migration. Share the checklist rules (see the strip finding) and the Refused class.
items.risk: Existing chart numbers must never change. The web booking's lock and unique key must keep working.
items.touches_owner_decision: none
items.proposal_final:
Keep the simplification, with the clinic's obligations written in:

1. **One chart-number rule.** One function, `nextChartNo(tx)`, used by:
   - Add patient (type.astro)
   - the forms queue and intake (patient-add.ts)
   - the calendar's new patient (api/schedule)
   - web booking (api/bookings)
   - the import's blank rows

   The rule: continue the clinic's own prefix and sequence when one prefix clearly dominates, for example SR-0144 → SR-0145. Otherwise fall back to P-0001 and up, stepping past every number already taken by `chartKey`.

   The safeguards:
   - Never renumber an existing patient or an imported chart number.
   - A number typed at the desk or brought in by the import still wins.
   - Every caller runs it after `lockClinic` (the existing book lock, same key) and inside the same transaction as the insert.
   - The unique key `(clinic_id, chart_no)` stays.
   - This replaces the web booking's count+1 (the open item in CLAUDE.md), so a deleted patient no longer blocks the next booking.

2. **One patient insert, `insertPatient(tx, ctx, fields)`.** It only inserts the patient row.
   - Each caller keeps its own consent write unchanged:
     - web: channel web, the notice in force, the IP, the visit
     - forms and intake: channel form or intake, the typed signature, as whom
     - desk: `recordDeskConsent` / `recordPaperConsent`
   - Each keeps its own attribution: `created_by` is a staff member at the desk, null for a patient's own answers, and `import_id` is set on imports.
   - Audit `patient.create` wherever a staff member did the insert, as the schedule path does today.

3. **Drop the unused tables.** Drop `form_template` and `form_response` in a new numbered migration; never edit schema.sql. The migration first refuses (raises) if either table has a single row. Production has been live since 24 Sep.

4. **One checklist.** Move the visit checklist's rules (panels.ts `fillCheck` and VisitStrip) into one pure module. Snapshot both screens before and after, and keep every line:
   - health history asked
   - blood pressure today
   - consent signed for THIS visit (`visit_treatment_consented`), and forms not agreed, with Go ahead anyway and its reason
   - under 18
   - clearance and lab case outstanding
   - statement, aftercare, next check-up

5. **One Refused class.** Replace the four page-local copies with `src/lib/refused.ts`.

Verify with paper-check, phone-e2e (all paths), choices-check, seat-check, a booking and a desk add at a clinic with SR- numbers, and a booking after a hand-deleted patient.

items.title: Make an HMO claim come from the statement, and let the payor's money land once
items.where: /c/<slug>/finances/new/ (HMO part), /c/<slug>/finances/?show=claims (New claim, Mark paid), /c/<slug>/finances/<id>/ (HMO payment), record → Treatment → HMO approvals (LOA); src/pages/c/[clinic]/finances/_claims.ts, _Claims.astro, src/lib/invoices.ts, src/lib/record-extra.ts, hmo_claim.invoice_id
items.problem: An HMO-covered treatment is three unlinked records: the LOA on the record, the HMO part on the statement, and a free-standing claim. hmo_claim.invoice_id exists but the app never sets it, so 0 of 4 seeded claims are linked. Measured: about 26 taps from LOA to money in. The amount is typed 4 times, the LOA number twice and the card number again. New claim makes the desk pick the patient from a 90-day list and retype what the statement already says. 'Mark paid' records no money, and its own help says: 'To put it against a patient's statement, record it there as an HMO or PhilHealth payment.' So one cheque from Intellicare is entered in two places, or the two disagree. Finances shows two HMO-owed figures that never reconcile: the Still to pay tile's 'more from HMOs' comes from statements, and the Overdue claims tile's '₱9,100 waiting' comes from claims. A partly approved or denied claim never changes what the patient owes. payor_share is frozen on the statement (trigger in 022), so the denied ₱900 stays 'from Medicard' forever unless the owner voids and charges again.
items.proposal: Saving a statement with an HMO or PhilHealth part creates its draft claim, linked (invoice_id), prefilled with the patient, the payor, the part, the card number from the patient row and the approval code of the record's approved LOA. The claims list then shows the statement number, and New claim stays only for claims with no statement (old visits). The claim's 'Mark paid' records the HMO/PhilHealth payment on the linked statement in the same transaction, with the amount approved, so 'paid' happens once and the drawer, the statement and the claim agree. Record answer becomes one 'Save the answer' button: the server calls it partly approved when the amount is below the claim. A denial or part-approval leaves a clear next step on the statement ('₱900 not covered by Medicard: now the patient's part'). How that is booked needs a rule, below.
items.risk: Statements are immutable by design. Moving a denied part to the patient needs an insert-only adjustment row (or a void-and-replace), not an update of payor_share, and patient_balance() and DUE_SQL must read it, or the one balance definition splits. Existing unlinked claims stay as they are (shown 'no statement'). Claim amounts stay behind finance.money.
items.touches_owner_decision: Who owes the part an HMO denies or cuts, and whether the app may move it to the patient's part on its own or only when the desk confirms. Also the 'statements are never edited' control.
items.proposal_final:
Make an HMO or PhilHealth claim come from its statement, and record the payor's money once.

1. Link the claim. Saving a statement with an HMO or PhilHealth part creates that statement's draft claim in the same transaction, linked by invoice_id and audited claim.new.
   - The claim is prefilled with the patient, the payor, the payor's part and the card number from the patient row.
   - The approval code is filled in only when exactly one approved LOA from that payor covers the plan lines charged on the statement (through procedure_id). Otherwise it is left blank. The app never guesses.
   - The claims list shows the statement number.
   - New claim stays only for claims with no statement, such as old visits. Existing unlinked claims show "no statement" and are left as they are.
   - Claim amounts stay behind finance.money.

2. Pay once. On a linked claim, Mark paid records the HMO or PhilHealth payment on the statement through recordPayment(), in the same transaction as the claim's change to paid.
   - It needs both finance.money and finance.bill.
   - It takes the amount approved, the day the money arrived (not today by default), the cheque or remittance reference, and the BIR receipt number box. The receipt number can still be written later with setBirRef.
   - It keeps recordPayment's lock, its cap at the balance, its form_key repeat check and the payment.record audit.
   - If recordPayment refuses (for example, the patient already paid in full), nothing is saved and the claim says so in one sentence. It is never marked paid alone.
   - Record answer becomes one "Save the answer" button. The server calls it partly approved when the amount is below what was claimed, and keeps every audit as today.

3. A denied or cut part. The app moves nothing by itself, and its words name no one as owing.
   - The statement and the claim show one plain line: "Medicard did not pay ₱900 of this statement." The desk then chooses what happens next.
   - Whatever the desk chooses is a new insert-only row: never an update of payor_share, and never a void of a statement that has payments. It carries a reason, who and when, and an audit entry.
   - patient_balance(), DUE_SQL, sumsOf() and buildLedger read that row (it shows on the Treatment record, and the last balance still equals patient_balance()).
   - For PhilHealth, the desk is shown the circular's cap from coverage.astro, and nothing is moved to the patient past it.
   - This rule needs a migration and is built only after the owner answers.

Question for the owner: "When an HMO or PhilHealth pays less than the statement expected, should the clinic be able to move the unpaid part onto what the patient owes (the desk confirms each time, with a reason), or keep it as money the clinic chases from the HMO or writes off, never billed to the patient?"

What to build:

- New charge: replace the Paid now checkbox and its fourth card with a choice at the total.

  - "Save, pays later" is quiet.

What must not change:
- Payment and statement: the statement and the payment are saved in one transaction (saveStatement's after: a refused payment saves nothing). The form keys (form_key, pay_key) and the Enter guard carry over. The audit entry stays payment.record.
- Payment methods: HMO and PhilHealth stay off checkout (PAYOR_METHODS) and stay on the statement page.
- Statement page: Record payment stays green (the owner, 26 Sep: "the one main action is Record payment, in green (money in)").
- The later BIR paths: Add BIR no. in each payment's side panel stays, because the booklet receipt is often written after the patient leaves (setBirRef). Correct, with its reason and the old number kept (fixBirRef, payment_bir_ref_change), stays too.
- The BIR wording: the field keeps "BIR invoice or receipt" in its label. The NOT_BIR line stays at the total and on the statement.

Help text:
- Cut only the lines that explain how to use the page, such as "Tap a service and it is added…" and "Record the payment with the statement in one go…".
- Keep every fact:
  - the fee guide's range;
  - the ID number printing on the statement;
  - "Filled in from statement X … Check the card";
  - the older-discount line;
  - the 60-or-over OSCA hint;
  - the HMO's part, "record it as paid when their money comes in";
  - "A saved statement is not edited … the owner or admin voids it";
  - NOT_BIR.

Risk: making payment the default could record money that was never received, and only the owner or admin can void that, with a reason. That is why the first tap only opens the fields and the second press names the amount and method.

The first 560 px are a payments table that always lists 8 methods, all ₱0.00 on a quiet day, including Cheque, which no new payment can use.
