items.proposal_final:
Close the day in the order the desk does it: settle, take stock, count, close.

Where: /c/<slug>/finances/close/ (src/pages/c/[clinic]/finances/close/index.astro), plus one href and its comment in src/pages/c/[clinic]/finances/index.astro.

On screen:
1. **Still open** comes first and shows only the groups with something in them. With none, it is one line: "Nothing left open." This puts the settling (Charge, Record payment, Rebook) before the count, so the desk does not have to close twice.
2. **Today's takings** shows only the methods used today, plus the total row.
   - Zero rows stay in the markup (data-zero) and are hidden on screen only, so the printed sheet still lists all eight methods every evening.
   - Under the table, for finance.money only, add a folded "Today's N payments" list: name, method, amount and statement no. Each row opens its statement, or the patient's account when the payment is on no statement.
   - The list opens when the page is reached at #payments.
   - Without finance.money the list is not drawn, so the blind count stays blind. The counts by method stay, as today.
3. **Count the drawer** with Close the day, unchanged. The blind path, the variance words and "close again" all stay as they are.
4. **Tomorrow** becomes one line: "Tomorrow: 6 visits, 2 not confirmed, 1 with no mobile — Calls". It is printed too, because the end-of-day brief asks for tomorrow's count and confirmations.

In Finances, the "Collected today" tile links to close/#payments (the Dashboard's tile already goes to close/). Update the tile comment.

Print stays a complete record: every method, every group (an empty one as a single "none" line), the payments list in full, the count and the signature line.

Expect, as measured by simulation:
- On a day with things open, the page is about 25% shorter (2195→1679 px at 1440, 2882→2297 px at 390), but Close sits lower, after the open items. That is intended.
- On a quiet day, Close comes up to about y=870 at 1440.

No migration and no change to who may see what. Re-measure contrast light and dark at 1440 and 390, and the printed sheet.

Effort: S.

items.title: A payment plan is not money owed today
items.where: record → Treatment → Braces and payment plans; /c/<slug>/finances/<id>/ (amount prefill); Finances Still to pay; Patients 'With balance'; Messages → Text a patient 'Owes' and the Balance template; src/lib/record-extra.ts (planState), src/lib/text-templates.ts, [invoice]/index.astro (defaultAmount)
items.problem: A plan makes one statement for the whole treatment (createStatement with the plan total), and only the record knows the schedule: planState computes dueNow and behind, and payment_plan is read nowhere else. So a braces patient who is up to date shows the whole remaining amount as owed on the Finances tile and the Still to pay list (oldest first, so plans sit at the top for months), in Patients → With balance, on the Dashboard panel's Balance, and in Messages' 'Owes' group. There the Balance template would text 'your account has a balance of ₱54,000'. On the statement page the amount prefills the whole remaining balance (defaultAmount = patientDue), not the installment, so each month the desk must retype it, and an Enter records the lot. New plan does not take the down payment, so that is a second trip to Finances.
items.proposal: Wherever a balance is shown or acted on, read the plan beside patient_balance(): 'On a plan · ₱3,000 due now (month 4 of 18)' or 'On a plan · up to date'. On the statement page of a plan, prefill what is due now and name the month. Leave not-yet-due plan money out of Still to pay's 'owes now' sense and out of the Balance text (or show it as 'on plans'). Let New plan take the down payment in the same step, with the same payment component as Paid now.
items.risk: Two ideas of 'owed' could drift. patient_balance() must stay the one balance, with 'due now' a view on top of it, and the Treatment record's balance (which must equal patient_balance()) unchanged. Clinics that lend informally may still want the full figure visible: show both, never hide the total.
items.touches_owner_decision: none (patient_balance() stays the one balance definition)
items.proposal_final:
Title: A payment plan is not money owed today.

Wherever a balance is shown or acted on, show the plan next to `patient_balance()`, never instead of it. The places are:
- Finances' tile and Still to pay
- Patients → With balance
- the Dashboard visit panel's Balance
- the record's Account line and its Braces and payment plans
- Messages → Text a patient "Owes"

Examples: "₱54,000 · on a plan · ₱3,000 due now (month 4 of 18)", or "₱54,000 · on a plan · up to date". The plan's state is worked out in one place only: `planState` in `record-extra.ts`, moved to a pure module that every page reads. `patient_balance()` stays the one balance, and the Treatment record's balance is unchanged (it must still equal `patient_balance()`).

1. **Still to pay.** Keep every plan on the list with its total. Sort and mark the list by what is due now, so a plan that is up to date sits below money that is overdue. Never leave a plan's statement off the list.
2. **The Balance text.** For a patient whose whole balance is on a plan that is up to date, don't offer it under "Owes" (or show them under "On a plan"). When an amount is due, fill `{amount}` with what is overdue and use words such as "a payment of PHP 3,000 is due on your plan". Keep the texts GSM-safe, with no link and no reply asked.
3. **The statement page of a plan.** Start the amount box at what is overdue (`behind`); if nothing is overdue, at the next instalment (`nextDueAmount`). Never above `patientDue`. Name the month ("month 4 of 18"). The desk can still type any amount, up to the whole balance.
4. **New plan takes the down payment** with the same payment component as Paid now (`saveStatement(…, after)`, in the plan's own transaction):
   - the same methods, reference and BIR invoice or receipt number field;
   - the same audit;
   - only for someone with `finance.bill`;
   - a refused payment rolls back the plan and its statement;
   - it lands on the payment's acknowledgment (`?done=paid&p=`) so the acknowledgment can be printed.
5. **Who sees amounts.** Every new line about a plan follows the page's existing amount gate (`finance.money` / `finance.bill`). Without it, a line says "on a plan" and shows no sum.

Risk: two ideas of "owed" could drift apart. Avoid that by keeping due-now as a view computed from the plan's schedule and the statement's payments, and by always showing the total next to it.

items.title: One word and one colour for what a patient owes
items.where: Finances list and tiles, statement page, record Account fold ([patient].astro STMT_TINT, text-caries), VisitPanels.astro, cal/panels.ts STMT_WORD, Close the day, Patients list, Messages
items.problem: The same quantity shows on 14 surfaces under 8 words: Still to pay, Owes/owed, Left, Balance, Still owed, Left owing, With balance, credit. An unpaid statement is 'Unpaid' in Finances and the record, 'Not paid yet' on the record's visit panel and 'not paid yet' on the Dashboard's. Finances draws owed money amber and keeps red for overdue (its own rule, in its code comments), but the record's Account fold draws 'Owes ₱2,400.00' in red (text-caries) and the Unpaid pill red (ws-tint-red). The fold also has two headings for one part ('Account', then 'Money').
items.proposal: Use one vocabulary from one module, like STATUS in invoices.ts. A statement is Unpaid · Part paid · Paid · Void everywhere, and the amount is 'Still to pay' for a statement and 'owes ₱X' for a person. Amber everywhere for owed and red only for overdue, with the record's Account fold matched to Finances. Drop the duplicate 'Money' heading. Keep 'Balance' only where the paper says it (the Treatment record column).
items.risk: Contrast must be re-measured where colours change (the record's paper sheets keep light tokens in both themes). Screen readers' sr-only words change with the visible ones.
items.touches_owner_decision: The paper record's own words: the PDA ledger column 'Balance' stays as the paper prints it.
items.proposal_final:
One word set and one colour rule for money a patient owes, from one module.

1. **Statement status.** Unpaid · Part paid · Paid · Void (and Draft) everywhere. This replaces "Not paid yet" in VisitPanels and "not paid yet" in `cal/panels.ts` `STMT_WORD`. Always keep the word beside its dot.
2. **Statement amount.** "Still to pay" everywhere. This replaces "Left" in the record's Account table and "Still owed" in the visit panel.
3. **A person's total.** "Owes ₱X" when positive, "In credit ₱X" when negative (kept as its own word: the clinic owes the patient), "Nothing owed" at zero.
4. **"Balance".** Only in the Treatment record's column, on screen and on its A4 paper.
5. **One source.** Put the words and tones in `STATUS` in `src/lib/invoices.ts`, and change its own tone first. Unpaid and Part paid become amber/warn; red only for overdue. Then delete the local copies: Finances' `TONE_OF`, the record's `STMT_TINT` and `BILL_STATUS` use, and panels.ts `STMT_WORD`.
6. **The record's Account fold.** Draw "Owes ₱X" and the Unpaid chip amber, not `text-caries` / `ws-tint-red` / `.pp-owed` red. Allergies stay the only red on the sheet.
7. **The duplicate heading.** Drop the visible "Money" pane heading under "Account", or make it sr-only "Account", following the record's rule that a card titled as its part keeps its title for a screen reader only. Keep the line "Statements of account, not BIR receipts." word for word.
8. **Screen readers.** Change the sr-only words along with the visible ones.
9. **Measure.** Amber on the paper sheet (`--pp-paper`, light tokens in both themes) and on every changed surface must reach at least 4.5:1, light and dark, at 1440 and 390. Print pages stay black on white.

items.title: Finances: let the tiles be the filters
items.where: /c/<slug>/finances/; finances/index.astro
items.problem: The first screen holds 15 controls at 1440: 4 tiles, 2 section tabs, New charge, Close the day, 4 pills, search and Download. The pieces repeat each other. The 'Still to pay' tile and the 'Still to pay' pill open the same list. The 'Overdue claims' tile and the 'HMO claims' tab open the same section. The 'Void' pill is a subset of 'All', which already includes void statements. 'Collected today' links nowhere here but to Close the day on the Dashboard. On a phone the tiles push the list down by about 280 px.
items.proposal: Three tiles that are also the switches: Today (collected · charged), Still to pay (the list), HMO claims (waiting · overdue). The selected tile is the chosen thing in teal tint. This drops the pills row and the separate section tabs; 'This month' becomes the owner's line under the tiles. Void stays findable through All, search and the CSV. Collected today opens Close the day.
items.risk: A different pattern from the shell's Tabs, so keyboard order and aria for tiles-as-tabs need care. Deep links (?view=, ?show=) must keep working.
items.touches_owner_decision: The owner's 26 Sep 2026 'Very simple' layout for Finances: four tiles, then one card with the two sections as tabs and the filters as one row of pills. Ask before changing it.

items.title: Give the owner the day's close, every day, in one place
items.where: /c/<slug>/finances/ (owner view), /c/<slug>/finances/close/; day_close
items.problem: Nothing shows a past close. The page reads day_close only for today, and the CSVs do not include it. The blind count promises that the expected figure and the difference are 'kept for the owner', but the owner has no screen where they appear after midnight. Whether the drawer matched yesterday, or whether the desk closed at all on Saturday, cannot be looked up. An owner of two branches (liwayway: session-road and marikina-heights) has to switch branch and open each Finances page to see each day.
items.proposal: For people with finance.money, one quiet card on Finances: 'Drawer, last 7 days: matched 5 · ₱200 short Tue (note) · not closed Sat', each day opening close/?day=<date> read-only. Later, a group line across branches for an owner with more than one.
items.risk: It adds a card to a screen we are trying to calm, so make it owner-only and one line when everything matched. ?day= must be read-only (the insert stays today-only).
items.touches_owner_decision: none
items.proposal_final:
Title: Make "kept for the owner" true. Show the last two weeks of drawer closes on Close the day, and link to it from the tile that already names it.

Where: /c/<slug>/finances/close/ (a new section after Count the drawer) and the Finances "Collected today" tile. No new card on Finances, and no migration.

Who: people with finance.money (by default the owner and the admin). The Secretary's blind count stays blind.

1. On close/, below Count the drawer, add one quiet section, "Earlier closes", shown only with finance.money. It has one line per day for the last 14 Manila days, newest first:
   - The date, who closed and when.
   - Counted against expected and the difference, in the page's own words (varianceWords: "Matches", "₱200 short", "₱50 over"), with the note.
   - A day closed more than once says so and lists every close, for example "Closed 2 times: ₱500 short at 6:10 pm, then Matches at 6:25 pm". Any close after the first is what the owner most needs to see.
   - "Not closed" appears only for a past day that had a non-void payment or a completed visit. A day the clinic was shut is never flagged.
   - If all 14 days matched, the section is one line: "Every day matched in the last 14 days."
   - It is read-only, has no ?day= view, and the insert stays today-only.
   - The section does not print with the day's sheet.

2. The Finances "Collected today" tile, which today links nowhere, links to close/, the same as the Dashboard's tile of the same name. It turns amber with one note, such as "Drawer ₱200 short Tue" or "Not closed Sat", only when a day in the last 7 has a difference or no close. Otherwise its note stays as it is.

3. For the owner, as a question: for an owner of two branches (liwayway: session-road and marikina-heights), is one line across branches worth a group-level read (a definer function), or is switching branch enough?

Impact 3, effort S–M.

Risks: keep the section under 44 px targets and ≥4.5:1 contrast in light and dark, as the rest of close/ is. Write "not closed" carefully so it does not accuse a day the clinic was closed.

Touches owner decision: none. This is a gap fix that keeps a promise the page already makes, not a simplification. List it that way in the plan.

items.title: One place for one patient's money: the record's Account
items.where: record → Account fold (#money), /c/<slug>/finances/?patient=<id>&view=all ('All of X's statements', 'In Finances', the who-line, Charge this patient); [patient].astro, finances/index.astro
items.problem: A patient's statements are listed by two separate implementations: the record's Account table (Statement · For · Total · Paid · Left · Status) and Finances filtered by ?patient= (its own 'Owes' line and 'Charge this patient'). The statement page's 'All of Maria Liza's statements' goes to the Finances version and the record's 'In Finances' goes there too. Neither the record nor the Finances filter has a way to take a payment: the desk opens a statement first (3 taps from the record). The visit panels and the Treatment record show the same statements a third and fourth way, which is fine because they are by visit.
items.proposal: Make the record's Account the one per-patient money view. Add a 'Take a payment' action there that opens the shared payment form on the oldest unpaid statement, point 'All of X's statements' to the record #money, and retire the Finances ?patient= mode (name search stays). That is one fewer code path to keep in step.
items.risk: Someone with finance.bill but without records access could no longer see a patient's statements in one list, so keep a minimal ?patient= list for them or give the Account fold to finance roles. Old links with ?patient= must still land somewhere sensible.
items.touches_owner_decision: none
items.proposal_final:
One place for one patient's money: the record's Account (the attached sheet #money, shown only with finance.bill as now).

1. On each row of the Account table that still has money left, add a quiet "Pay" link to that statement's own payment form (/c/<slug>/finances/<id>/#pay). That is one tap from the open sheet instead of three. Never pick the statement automatically: the desk chooses which statement a payment is for, because the acknowledgment, the BIR invoice or receipt number, the HMO or PhilHealth share and the Treatment record's per-visit balance all follow that link. No new teal button: New booking stays the record's one teal.
2. Keep the sheet's line "Statements of account, not BIR receipts." Add the HMO or PhilHealth part still due to the sheet's one money line ("Owes ₱X · ₱Y more from Maxicare"), the way the Finances patient line shows it today.
3. Point the statement page's "All of <name>'s statements" and the sheet's own "In Finances" (drop it, or keep it for the clinic-wide list) to the record at #money, with the Account sheet opened.
4. Retire the Finances ?patient= mode by redirecting old ?patient= links to the record's #money. Keep the finance.bill gate, which still refuses anyone without it. Name, chart number and statement number search in Finances stays. Keep "Charge this patient" as the sheet's existing New charge.
5. Do not suppress or merge the record's 'patient.view' audit for these looks. A money lookup now opens the clinical record, so it should be logged as one. Land on #money so the front-desk screen shows the money sheet rather than the health history.
Check: the last balance on the sheet still equals patient_balance(); contrast of at least 4.5:1, light and dark, at 1440 and 390; Pay links at least 44px tall; a secretary (finance.bill without finance.money) sees exactly what Finances showed them before.

items.title: Correct a statement in one step: Replace
items.where: /c/<slug>/finances/<id>/ (More → Void, each payment's More → Void), /finances/new/; src/lib/invoices.ts (voidPayment, voidStatement, createStatement)
items.problem: A wrong price or patient needs each payment voided first, then the statement, then the whole charge typed again, then the payment taken again. That is about 14 taps, 2 typed reasons and 3 screens, and only the owner or admin can start it, so the desk waits. Nothing carries over: the lines, discount ID and HMO part are retyped from memory.
items.proposal: 'Replace this statement' (owner/admin): one reason, then New charge opens prefilled with the same patient, lines, discount and HMO part. On save, one transaction voids the old statement and its payments with that reason and records the same payments on the new statement, each pointing at the one it replaces, so the drawer, the acknowledgments and the audit all stay true. Optionally the desk proposes and the owner approves with one tap.
items.risk: It must never look like an edit: the old number stays used and shows void, and the audit names both. Moving payments changes which statement an already-printed acknowledgment names, so print a fresh acknowledgment or note the replacement on it.
items.touches_owner_decision: The standing control 'a saved statement is not edited: the owner or admin voids it and you charge again', and whether the desk may start a replacement for the owner to approve.
items.proposal_final:
"Replace this statement" on `/c/<slug>/finances/<id>/` → More, for whoever holds `finance.void` (the owner and admin by default; the owner can tick it for the desk on the Roles screen). There is no approval queue. The person types one reason (`REASON_MIN`/`MAX`). New charge then opens prefilled with:
- the patient, which can be changed;
- the lines, each keeping its `procedure_id`;
- the discount kind and ID number, with the existing "check the card" line still shown;
- the HMO or PhilHealth payor and share;
- the payments to move, listed read-only.

On Save, one transaction:
1. Voids each live payment, then the statement, with that reason, through the existing `voidPayment` and `voidStatement`. The triggers stay unchanged.
2. Creates the new statement through `createStatement` under its lock. It gets the next SOA number; the series has no gaps.
3. Inserts each moved payment as a new row with the same `method`, `amount`, `reference` and `paid_on` (the original day, so no day's drawer total moves).

An additive migration adds `invoice.replaces_id` and `payment.replaces_id`. Screens and papers then say "Replaces SOA-12" and "Replaced by SOA-15 on <day>: <reason>". A moved payment's line and its acknowledgment say "Received by <original receiver> on <day>; moved from SOA-12 payment 1 by <name>". The audit adds `invoice.replace`, naming both statements, beside the usual void, create and record rows.

Refusals and guards:
- **Too much paid.** If the moved payments exceed the new total, refuse: "₱X more than this statement was paid. Void a payment and give it back first."
- **BIR receipt number.** Carry `bir_ref` only when the patient is the same. Otherwise leave it blank and say: "BIR receipt <no> was issued for <old patient>. Correct it in your booklet and write the new number here."
- **Payment plans and claims.** Refuse Replace on a statement a payment plan is built on, or one whose HMO or PhilHealth claim is filed or later, and say why. Those keep the long way. Today's void has no such guard either, so add the same check to `voidStatement`.
- **Acknowledgments already printed.** Afterwards the page offers Print the new acknowledgment. An old acknowledgment prints as void, "replaced by SOA-15".
- **Disclaimer.** The `NOT_BIR` line stays on every paper.

items.title: Print with one button
items.where: /c/<slug>/finances/<id>/ (Print menu, each payment's Print, the success line's 'Print the acknowledgment'), /finances/<id>/print/ (A5 · 80 mm toggle); [invoice]/index.astro, [invoice]/print.astro
items.problem: The paper size is chosen twice: the statement page's Print menu asks A5 or 80 mm, then the print page shows the same A5 / 80 mm toggle and its own Print. There are three Print entry points on one statement: the menu, each payment's Print, and the success line. Printing the acknowledgment after a payment is 2 taps plus the browser dialog.
items.proposal: One quiet 'Print' on the statement and one 'Print' on each payment, both opening the print page. The print page keeps the A5 / 80 mm toggle and remembers the choice per device (localStorage, as a convenience only). Drop the menu.
items.risk: localStorage can be empty in a private window, so the default stays A5. Nothing else changes on paper.
items.touches_owner_decision: none
items.proposal_final:
Print with one button. On /c/<slug>/finances/<id>/:
- Replace the Print menu (A5 paper / 80 mm receipt) with one quiet "Print" link to print/.
- Keep each payment's quiet Print, which opens print/?ack=<id>.
- Keep the success line's "Print the acknowledgment" after a payment, and "Print the statement" after a new statement. That line is the documented checkout path (Paid now lands on ?done=paid&p=…) and is one tap.
- The payment side panel's "Print the acknowledgment" may stay.

The print page keeps:
- its A5 / 80 mm pills and its one teal Print;
- writing one audit row per load (payment.print or invoice.print);
- the NOT_BIR line, the BIR invoice or receipt no., and every word on the paper, unchanged.

Remember the paper per device so the server draws the right size on the first load, without a client-side redirect or reload. A redirect would write a second audit row and flash the wrong size. Do it this way:
- Choosing a pill sets a small first-party cookie scoped to /c/ (for example fl_paper=a5|receipt, a year, no personal data).
- print.astro uses that cookie when ?paper is absent. An explicit ?paper always wins.
- With no cookie (private window, cleared), the default stays A5.

Nothing else changes on paper. To check:
- The menu is gone, and the statement page has one quiet Print.
- A receipt choice persists across statements on the same browser.
- One print writes exactly one audit_log row.
- The success-line link still lands on the acknowledgment.
- 44 px targets, contrast ≥ 4.5:1 light and dark at 1440 and 390.

items.title: Claims: one answer button and one claims page
items.where: Claim side panel (Record answer), /c/<slug>/claims/ vs /c/<slug>/finances/?show=claims; _Claims.astro, claims/index.astro, _claims.ts
items.problem: The answer form has one amount box and two buttons, 'Approved' and 'Partly approved'. Its help tells the user which to press from the number they typed ('All of it: Approved. Less than was claimed: Partly approved'). The same list is drawn by two pages with different tiles (2 vs 4), a different URL key (view= vs claims=) and a 307 redirect between them, only so a dentist can read claims and add notes.
items.proposal: One 'Save the answer'; the server derives approved or partly approved from the amount. Ask the owner whether dentists need the claims list at all. If yes, render the same component and tiles under one route with amounts hidden. If no, drop /claims/ for non-finance staff and its sidebar link.
items.risk: Someone who relies on the dentist's note on a claim loses it if /claims/ goes, which is why it is a question. Old /claims/ links must keep redirecting.
items.touches_owner_decision: Whether dentists and assistants without Finances should see HMO claims (it was in everyone's menu before the three tabs).
items.proposal_final:
Claims: one answer button, and one claims list drawn the same way everywhere.

1. **Record answer gets one button.** Keep one amount box and one teal "Save the answer". Keep "Denied" as its own form with its reason.
   - The server decides the status from the amount: equal to the claim means approved (sets resolved_at, as today); less means partly_approved (no resolved_at, as today); more is refused, using today's sentence.
   - Each save still writes one audit_log row ('approve' or 'partly', matching the status chosen) under the claim's row lock and the "missed" re-check.
   - CLAIM_DONE's two notices stay.
   - Drop the help line that tells people which button to press.
   - Existing claims and the CSV are unchanged.

2. **Ask the owner before touching dentists' access:** "Should dentists and assistants without Finances still see the HMO and PhilHealth claims list (patients, payor, status, aging and notes, no amounts), or only the people who handle money?"
   - **If yes:** keep /claims/ as their route. Never open /finances/ to people without finance.bill. Make the two pages identical apart from amounts: the same component, the same view key (claims=), and the same tiles less the money ones. The 307 redirect for finance users stays, keeping its query and POST body.
   - **If no:** take /claims/ and its sidebar link away from people without Finances. For them, /claims/ answers with a plain "Claims are in Finances" (or the Dashboard). For finance users it keeps redirecting as today.
   - In both cases, existing notes and audit rows stay. Re-run the 030 role snapshot (snap.mjs / cmp.mjs over the 7 roles) afterwards.

items.title: Flossify's own plan: say it once, and only when it matters
items.where: Workspace sidebar strip (src/components/BillingNotice.astro, src/components/ws/plan.ts, src/lib/billing.ts describe()), /c/<slug>/settings/#plan (PlanSection.astro)
items.problem: For the whole 30-day trial, every workspace page for the owner and admin carries a blue card in the sidebar, 'Trial: 30 days left. Your Flossify plan'. On the plan section the trial is said 4 times (strip, callout, tile note, nav item), and that the prices are not final 3 times (amber callout, 'Not final yet' tile, the empty invoices line).
items.proposal: Show the strip only in the last 7 days of the trial or when an invoice is due or overdue, which is what the component's own comment says: 'nothing is drawn … most days'. On the plan section, one status line, with 'Prices are not final: you will not be charged until we tell you' once, and the tiles without repeating it.
items.risk: Fewer reminders of the trial may surprise an owner when it ends. The last-7-days line covers it.
items.touches_owner_decision: How visible the trial and the 'prices not final' notice should be (BILLING_FINAL placeholders); the notice itself stays.
items.proposal_final:
Title: Flossify's own plan: say it once, and only when it matters.

Where: src/lib/billing.ts describe() (or src/components/ws/plan.ts), src/components/BillingNotice.astro, and settings/_ui/PlanSection.astro.

1) The sidebar strip (BillingNotice) appears only when one of these is true:
- The trial has 7 days or fewer left.
- The trial has ended. Show this for 7 days after the end, so the line doesn't stay on every page forever while BILLING_FINAL is false.
- The subscription is cancelled.
- Any invoice is 'due'. This includes the "Invoice … was made before the prices were final. Do not pay it" line, which always shows while such an invoice exists.

On the other trial days nothing is drawn, which is what the component's own comment says. The Plan link in the sidebar or the person menu is still how to reach the plan. The plan page still says the days left in the "Each month" tile ("Trial: N days left · ends <date>").

2) The plan section (#plan) says "not final" once, as a callout, and the trial once, in the tile:
- One callout: "Prices are not final: you will not be charged until we tell you." It is drawn once.
- The trial callout (v.notice) is not drawn when it only repeats the trial line, because the "Each month" tile already says it. Still draw v.notice when it is about an invoice, the trial having ended, or a cancellation.
- KEEP the two words "Not final yet" on the "Per branch, a month" tile. CLAUDE.md says every price is labelled "not final yet" while BILLING_FINAL is false, so a placeholder price never travels without its label.
- KEEP the invoice pills "Do not pay: prices not final".
- With no invoices, the empty line says just "No invoices yet." The callout already says nothing is charged.

Measure before and after for the owner of session-road at 1440×900 and 390×844:
- The sidebar's height and the controls in the first screen on the Dashboard.
- How many times "trial" and "not final" appear on #plan.

Then check the same page with a planted 'due' invoice (on a scratch database, never the shared seed) and with trial_ends_at 5 days ahead, to confirm the strip still appears in both.

Risk: an owner sees the trial reminder less often. Nothing is charged while BILLING_FINAL is false, and the last-7-days line plus the tile cover the end of the trial.

items.title: The not-BIR line on paper, not on every screen
items.where: Finances list foot, New charge total card, statement Charges card, record Account fold, and all prints; NOT_BIR in src/lib/invoices.ts
items.problem: 'Flossify is not a BIR-registered invoicing system. The clinic's BIR invoice or receipt is a separate paper.' is drawn on 4 everyday screens (plus 'Statements of account, not BIR receipts' on the record) as well as on every printed statement and acknowledgment. The desk reads the same 20 words at every checkout.
items.proposal: Keep it on every paper and once on screen, on New charge beside Save. Drop it from the Finances list, the statement page and the record.
items.risk: This is BIR-related wording that protects the clinic. Removing it from a screen is a legal call, not a design call.
items.touches_owner_decision: BIR-related wording: the owner (and their accountant or lawyer) decides where the not-BIR statement must appear.
items.proposal_final:
Ask the owner, not a change. Keep NOT_BIR, word for word, on every printed paper: the statement, the acknowledgment, and the A4 Treatment record when money is shown. On screen, show it once, on New charge, under the teal Save statement. That is where the desk makes the statement, and so where "issue the clinic's own BIR invoice too" applies.

Drop three things:

items.problem: Tapping one service opens 'Edit prices' with all 14 services (70 fields, 73 controls, content 3313 px = 3.8 panel heights) and saves all 70. Add and Edit are two different forms: Add has name, kind, price, minutes, local name, unit, code; Edit has price, up to, minutes, offered, 'from' — so a misspelt name, wrong kind or unit cannot be corrected after adding, and nothing can be removed (only 'Offered' off).
items.proposal: One 'Service' panel for both: name, kind, price, up to, minutes, offered, 'Show as from', and local name/unit/code under More. Code stays fixed once made (chart_effect and data.ts read it).
items.risk: Renaming a service must not change past statements or the code that chart_effect and the reason lookup use (rename the label only). A one-row save must keep saveFees' validation (price ≤ up to, minutes).
items.touches_owner_decision: none
items.proposal_final:
One "Service" panel for both Add and Edit. It holds name, kind, price, up to, minutes, Offered and "Show as from ₱…", with local name, unit and code under More. Tapping a row opens that service only and saves that row. Add opens the same panel empty. A compact "All prices" table stays as the quiet secondary action for setting up the whole guide in one pass: one line per service with price, up to, minutes and Offered, using saveFees as it is now. Nothing is ever deleted; Offered off still retires a service.

Safeguards for the one-service save, all in one withClinic transaction:
1. **Same checks.** Keep saveFees' checks: price is a number of zero or more, up to is not below the price, minutes are 5 to 480, and the cap on the largest price. Add addFee's checks for name and kind.
2. **Code fixed.** The code cannot be changed once the service is made. chart_effect, aftercare and booking all read it.
3. **Rename the label only.** Before changing the name, fill `procedure_done.name` with the old name wherever it is null for that catalog_id. That way no past treatment changes its words on the record, the Treatment record or its paper. Statement lines (frozen), plan lines, visit reasons and signed consent forms already keep their own copy. Say in the panel that past visits and statements keep the old name. Expect that visits booked before a service was recorded, which are matched by name, stop showing a price on the calendar after a rename. Either accept that or match the old name too.
4. **Unit and tooth_scoped.** If the unit is editable, recompute `tooth_scoped` from it as addFee does, or keep `tooth_scoped` unchanged and say so.
5. **Audit by service.** Audit `catalog.update` with `entity_id` set to the service.
6. **Kind changes change suggestions.** A change of name or kind changes the consent forms and aftercare sheet suggested for that service. Show the suggested forms in the panel (they are suggestions only) so the change is visible.

items.title: Days off in one form, and a dentist's time away shown on her page
items.where: Settings → Closed days (_ui/ClosedSection.astro, _lib/closed-days.ts) and the Dashboard's Block time (components/ws/cal/BlockPanel.astro, /api/schedule/blocks); person page Days pane
items.problem: 'The clinic is closed' and 'A dentist is away' are added from two different forms with the same words: Settings → Closed days (whole days, form post) and the calendar's Block time (whole days or from a time, plus a chair out of use, JSON). A dentist's availability lives in three places: her days and hours on her person page, her leave in Closed days or Block time, and nothing on her page says she is away next week.
items.proposal: One add form: Closed days' 'Add' opens the calendar's Block panel (same component, same API, same 'visits already inside' answer); the settings section keeps the list of everything ahead with Remove. On a dentist's person page, under Days at this branch, list her time away ahead (read from loadBlocks, scope her) with 'Add time away' opening the same panel pre-set to her.
items.risk: The settings form works with scripts off; the Block panel is script-driven. Keep a no-script fallback (the current form) or accept the change. Both must keep the book's lock and audit lines (schedule.block).
items.touches_owner_decision: 040 blocked time (unchanged rules; one form instead of two).
items.proposal_final:
Days off in one form, and a dentist's time away shown on her page.

1. **One add form.** Settings → Closed days' Add and the Dashboard's Block time both open the same Block time panel (`BlockPanel.astro`, POST /api/schedule/blocks). The panel already handles three cases: whole days or from a set time, the clinic closed, and a chair out of use.
   - Settings keeps the list of every block ahead. Remove stays a plain form post, so it works without scripts.
   - Pick one of two ways to handle scripts being off: keep today's whole-day form inside `<noscript>`, or accept that adding needs scripts, as the calendar already does.
   - The panel's code has to be lifted out of the calendar's `panels.ts`, where it is tied to the visit, booking and patient panels. That makes the effort M to L.

2. **The dentist's page.** On a dentist's person page, under Days at this branch, list her time away ahead and the clinic's closures. Read them with `upcomingBlocks` / `loadBlocks`, limited to her.
   - People with `people.manage` get Add time away, which opens the same panel already set to "A dentist is away" and her name. Each row also gets a Remove.
   - She sees the list read-only on her own page.

3. **Permissions, written down rather than moved.** Adding or removing a dated block is allowed to anyone with `schedule.edit` OR `settings.edit`. Both the API and each page check this on the server, so no role loses an ability it has today. The person page's buttons also need `people.manage`. Re-run the 7-role × 20-page snapshot (`snap.mjs` / `cmp.mjs`).

4. **Which dentists can be marked away.** The panel offers the dentists `isDentistHere` / `dentistsHere` allows, not only the calendar's columns. That way an owner who treats but has no column can still be marked away.

5. **Nothing changes in `blocks.ts`.** The book's lock, the audit lines (schedule.block, schedule.unblock), `holdClosedReminders` (044), the list of visits already booked inside, and the rule that nothing is texted, moved or cancelled all stay as they are. Calls → In closed time keeps listing those visits.

items.proposal_final:
QUESTION for the owner (040 left this to you). If the answer is yes:

Under Clinic settings → Closed days, add a "This year's holidays" list. Each line has its date and its kind. Regular holidays start ticked. items.title: A member who works at two branches: give the same account another branch
items.where: Add member (_lib/people.ts addPerson: emailTaken/phoneTaken across the service, usernameTaken per group; the only staff_access insert is for a new staff row), person page
items.problem: Nothing in the product gives an existing member access to a second branch: staff_access rows are only made with a new account. At Liwayway's group (session-road + marikina-heights), adding Dr. Sarmiento at Session Road by her email or mobile is refused ('already on a Flossify staff account'), and her username is taken in the group, so the only way is a second account with another username and no email or mobile — which then cannot reset by text.
items.proposal: On a person's page (for owners and admins of a multi-branch group): 'Works at' with a tick per branch of the group; ticking adds staff_access (no new account, same password, days set per branch on that branch's page). In Add member, when the email or mobile belongs to someone in this group, offer 'Add {name} to this branch' instead of the refusal.
items.risk: Rank rules (mayManage) and the per-branch money switch must apply at the new branch; audit the grant. Only within the same group; the global one-email/one-mobile rule stays.
items.touches_owner_decision: 'One email and one mobile per staff account across the whole service' — kept; this makes it workable for groups.
items.proposal_final:
A person's page in Clinic settings gets a **Works at** pane. It is shown only in a group with more than one branch, and only to someone who holds people.manage. It has one tick per branch of the group:
- **Who can tick.** You can tick or untick only a branch you have access to yourself.
- **Server checks for a tick** (staff_access insert), in this order: the person and the branch are in the same group (staff.group_id = clinic.group_id); you have people.manage at that branch; mayManage(you, them); mayGive(you, their current role). Their role is group-wide and applies at the new branch, so you cannot hand out a role you could not give.
- **What a new branch starts with.** can_edit_records follows the role, can_manage_staff comes from the role's perms (as addPerson sets it), and can_view_finance starts false. Only an owner turns it on, on that branch's page of the person.
- **Days.** Their days at the new branch are set on that branch's page, under "Days at this branch". No days are copied.
- **Audit.** Every tick and untick is an audit_log row in the target branch's clinic transaction (staff.access_add / staff.access_remove).
- **Untick.** This removes access only. Nothing they did there is deleted. It is refused for their home branch and for their last branch: use Disable instead. It is also refused while they are the dentist on visits ahead at that branch, and the refusal names how many visits to move first.

In **Add member**, when the email or mobile typed belongs to someone in THIS group who cannot open this branch, the form offers "{name} already has an account in {group}. Add them to {branch}". This runs the same checks as the tick. Their role, password, username, email and mobile stay as they are; nothing is created and no code is sent. When the email or mobile belongs to an account in another group, today's refusal stays word for word and names nobody. The rule of one email and one mobile per account across the service is unchanged.

Check: sign in as Liwayway and add Dr. Sarmiento at session-road from her marikina-heights account. She then opens /session-road/sign-in/ with the same password, and the branch switcher lists both branches. Her PRC status and public profile stay a single row. An admin cannot add the owner or a higher role. A session-road-only admin cannot tick marikina-heights. Finances stays off at the new branch, the audit rows land at the target branch, and untick is refused while she has visits ahead there.

Lead each setting with the question the owner is answering, keep one accurate line under it, and fold the rest behind a small "How this works". Words only: no change to any field name, value, default or behaviour.

- **How the day runs → Reminders.** "A visit ends up in closed time (you added lunch, a closed day or a dentist's leave after it was booked): [ ] Don't send its reminder until someone keeps or moves it on Calls." Folded: "Off: the reminder goes as usual."

- **Texts to patients.** Keep "The reminder the day before every visit always goes." Then: "[ ] A second reminder two days before" and "[ ] Text patients when their check-up is due (Tuesday or Wednesday morning, at most once every two months)." Folded: "from two weeks before it is due until two months after; the text names your number and asks them to call."
- **Time between visits.** Keep the one line as it is ("Online booking and the calendar's suggested times leave this after each visit. The desk can still book back to back.").
- **Roles intro.** "What each role may do. People can only give roles below their own." Folded: "A change counts for everyone who holds the role on their next click."
- **RoleField.** Keep "A dentist: needs a PRC licence, gets a column on the schedule and a public profile" visible. Shorten only the first line, to "What they may do comes with the role (Clinic settings → Roles)".
- **Tablets.** Intro: "A tablet where patients fill in their details and sign consent forms. It holds no staff sign-in." Keep "It signs this browser out of Flossify" beside the action that does it.

- Re-run choices-check.mjs and profile-check.mjs.

items.title: Two separate 'the patient fills it in' systems, each with its own queue, page, reference and 'Easiest' label
items.where: /c/<slug>/patients/new/ (chooser), /patients/new/type/ (second chooser), /patients/forms/ + /patients/qr/ + /f/<key>/ (028 QR poster), /patients/intake/ + /patients/intake/<id>/ + /f/i/<token>/ + /f/t/ (039 intake); src/lib/patient-forms*.ts, intake*.ts, src/components/ws/inbox.ts
items.problem: A desk adding a patient meets two choosers with different options. /patients/new/ marks 'On their phone' Easiest (a per-patient QR code, 039) and lists 4 'Other ways'. The next screen, /patients/new/type/, repeats a three-way header that marks 'Patients fill it in' Easiest (the desk poster, 028). The two systems then keep separate queues: 'New patient forms' (counted in the Inbox and on the Patients tab) and 'Patient forms in progress -> Sent: add to the records' (counted nowhere; inbox.ts has no intake count, and the reach crawl found no link to /patients/intake/). They also have two public form pages (/f/[key] 678 lines + _forms.css 249; /f/i/[token] 893 + _intake.css 116), two reference prefixes (QR-…, IN-…) and three health-history condition lists (CONDITIONS in patient-forms-def.ts; PAPER_CONDITIONS 23 + DESK_CONDITIONS in paper-history.ts; 27 ticks on the typed form). The phone intake takes up to 6 desk screens; the poster takes 0 before and 2 after.
items.proposal: Short term (S): count sent intakes in the Inbox and on the Patients tab beside poster forms. Show both in one queue, 'Forms to add', with one reference style. Drop the typed page's own three-way header so there is one chooser with three ways (Their phone · At the clinic · Type it in), and keep Import and the poster as links under it. Long term (L, question for the owner): make the desk poster an entry to the same intake engine (/f/<key>/ starts an intake for an unknown patient), so there is one public form, one page 1, one condition list (paper-history's, with aliases), one queue and one way to add to the records.
items.risk: Both paths carry consent and privacy rules: FORMS_PRIVACY_VERSIONS keeps the poster closed in production, and CONSENT_REVIEWED keeps the intake's forms closed. Merging must not open either before the lawyer has read the notice. Forms already submitted must stay readable under their old references, and the 30-day purge rules differ per path.
items.touches_owner_decision: The owner asked for both: the desk QR poster (028, 'second of the three and marked Easiest') and the step-by-step intake (039, including the owner's four answers). Which one is the patient's way should be put to the owner as a question. Also touches the RA 10173 informed-consent closure in FORMS_PRIVACY_VERSIONS.
items.proposal_final:
Short term (S, no owner decision touched):

(a) **Inbox and Patients tab.** Count sent intakes (`intake.status = 'sent'`, the same `countSentIntakes`) in the Inbox and on the Patients tab beside the poster forms. Show both counts only to people who can add patients (`canEditRecords`), as the forms count is shown today.

(b) **One list, "Forms to add".** List poster forms and sent intakes together. Each row:
- keeps the reference it was issued (QR-… or IN-…), never renumbered;
- says which way it came and when it will be deleted under its own rule (a poster form 30 days after it was sent; a sent intake 30 days after Send unless held);
- opens its existing add page, so each path's add logic, look-alike check (Screen F), consent signings and seal chain stay as they are.

Merge the list, not the add code.

(c) **One chooser.** Draw one chooser on whichever page the desk lands. On a server where consent forms are offered, that is Their phone · At the clinic · Type it in. Import a spreadsheet and the desk poster are quiet links under it. Where /patients/new/ redirects to ./type/ (production until CONSENT_REVIEWED is filled), the typed page keeps one header with Import and the poster, so Import stays reachable on the live site. Never show two "Easiest" labels.

Long term (L): only if the owner says yes to the question below. Make /f/<key>/ start an intake for an unknown patient, so there is one public form engine, one page 1 and one queue. Conditions:
- Only page 1 and the general consent run from a poster scan. Procedure forms still wait for the desk to tick them and the named dentist to record "I explained this".
- The poster path stays closed in production while FORMS_PRIVACY_VERSIONS is empty, and the forms while CONSENT_REVIEWED is empty.
- Forms already submitted stay readable under their old QR- references.
- Any change to the patient's questions is a new FORM_VERSION and keeps every condition asked today. It does not shrink to paper-history's 23. The dentist reads it in the review pack.

Question for the owner: Patients can fill in their own forms two ways today. One is the desk poster: anyone scans it, and the form waits until the desk adds it. The other is a QR code made for one patient: the desk ticks the consent forms first, and the record is made when the patient sends. Should the desk poster become the start of the same step-by-step forms, so there is one set of patient forms and one list to add from? If yes, should a poster patient's record be made when they send (as with the per-patient code), or wait for the desk to add it (as the poster works now)?

items.title: Too many places say what is waiting, and the Dashboard draws each of today's patients three times
items.where: src/layouts/Clinic.astro (Inbox, 5 rows), /c/<slug>/ (tiles, Next for you, tasks card, website lane, calendar, Today's patients), /calls/, /messages/, /patients/forms/, /patients/intake/, Patients 'Needs attention', /finances/close/
items.problem: Work waiting for the desk is spread over at least 11 places. The Inbox has failed texts, replies, web requests, closed time and poster forms, but not sent intakes. Calls has To confirm, Call back and In closed time. Messages has Failed and Replies. Then the Patients tab count, Needs attention, the intake list, the tasks card, the website lane, Finances 'Still to pay' and Close the day 'still open'. Messages and Tasks are 2 clicks away, reachable only from menus. On the Dashboard (1144px, 33 controls in the first screen) each patient appears in Next for you, on the calendar card and in Today's patients, so 'Allergy: Penicillin' is printed twice for one patient.
items.proposal: 1) Make the Inbox one 'Waiting for you' list covering every source: add sent intakes, tasks due today, visits to confirm for tomorrow and statements left owing today, each with a count and a link (S/M). 2) Question for the owner: from 1280px, show Today's patients only where the calendar is a list (phones), since Next for you and the calendar cards already carry name, allergies and the one-tap step. The Calls button moves to the calendar's toolbar.
items.risk: Today's patients holds the one-tap step and the minutes waited. Removing it on desktop must keep both on the calendar card. Owners who rely on the list could lose an at-a-glance view, so offer it as a toggle first.
items.touches_owner_decision: The Dashboard as a dentist-owner's home (3 Oct: Next for you, the slim strip, the tasks card only while open) and the four tabs (standing). Hiding Today's patients on desktop is a question for the owner, not a change.
items.proposal_final:
Too many places say what is waiting. Make the inbox the one list.

1) Turn the top bar's Inbox (src/layouts/Clinic.astro + src/components/ws/inbox.ts) into one "Waiting for you" list. Each row has a count and a link, and each new row uses its own page's gate inside the same withClinic transaction:
- Sent intakes waiting for the desk: records.edit plus canEditRecords, the intake list's own rule.
- Tasks due today or overdue: only the viewer's own tasks and the ones they gave.
- Tomorrow's visits still to confirm: Calls' rule.
- Statements left owing today: finance.bill. Counts only; no peso amounts unless the viewer has finance.money.
Keep the existing rules: no reset or invite codes counted or shown, forms only for records.edit, closed time only for schedule.edit. Leave out any row the viewer cannot open, never show it as 0. Effort S/M.

2) Also link Calls from the calendar's toolbar, so it is no longer reachable only through Today's patients.

3) Keep Today's patients on every width. Measured at 1440: calendar cards carry only an alert icon with the allergy in a hover title, and no step button. Next for you is one patient and only for someone who treats. So Today's patients is the only place the desk sees every patient's allergies and alerts in words, the one-tap step with the consent-form check at In the chair, the minutes waited and the desk note. The allergy shown in both Next for you and Today's patients is intended safety redundancy and stays.

If the Dashboard needs to be shorter later, any proposal must first put the allergy and alert words (not just an icon), the step and the desk note on the calendar card. It must then measure contrast and 44px targets, and only after that ask the owner about the list.

items.title: The paper record is still the heaviest screen: 180 controls, 53 plus marks, 3 teal buttons, consent drawn in 5 places
items.where: /c/<slug>/patients/<id>/ ([patient].astro 1629 lines, _record/ 31 files 4543 lines, record.css 1070 lines)
items.problem: Measured on SR-0142: 4447px tall at 1440 and 7179px at 390, 180 controls (37 in the first screen), 47 headings, about 1000 words, 19 side panels, 13 folds, 53 plus marks and 12 contents links. 3 teal buttons sit on the page (New booking, the health history's Save, DeskConsent's Record consent). The h2s 'Chart' and 'Treatment record' are each drawn twice. 'Treatment' (the attached plan sheet) sits next to 'Treatment record' (page 3) in the contents. Consent is drawn on page 2, in the visit panel's cards, as Treatment record rows, on the form's own page and in the attached sheets. A real paper form has no plus signs; the owner's latest ask was 'simple, uneventful but effective'.
items.proposal: Questions for the owner, each measurable with paper-check: (a) replace the per-box pluses with one quiet 'Edit' per section of the sheet (paper forms have none), keeping the box-as-button behaviour behind it; (b) rename the attached 'Treatment' sheet 'Treatment plan', and show planned items as greyed rows on page 3 rather than as a separate sheet; (c) make the health form's Save and Record consent quiet so New booking stays the one teal; (d) draw each consent once (page 2) and link to it from the visit panel instead of redrawing cards; (e) drop the visually hidden duplicate h2s.
items.risk: The pluses were an explicit owner ask (2 Oct). Hiding them behind Edit costs one more click for frequent edits, so measure the edit tasks before and after. Consent must stay visible wherever a dentist decides to treat (the visit panel), so a link must not hide a gap; keep the amber gap line.
items.touches_owner_decision: The record as a paper chart (3–4 Oct, standing) and the plus beside every editable detail (owner, 2 Oct). Items (a) and (d) are questions for the owner; (b), (c) and (e) keep the paper look.
items.proposal_final:
The paper record (/c/<slug>/patients/<id>/), measured on SR-0142 at 1440: 33 boxes are buttons with a plus mark, plus 20 .rec-plus marks (6 visible). Two teal buttons are visible: New booking, and Record consent, which appears only while privacy consent is missing. Two sheet titles have a screen-reader-only twin.

(a) Question for the owner: keep the boxes tappable (one tap still opens Edit details with the caret in that field) but replace the 53 plus marks with one quiet "Edit" per section of the sheet, as a printed form would look. Afterwards, run paper-check and count the taps for the edit tasks before and after.

(b) Rename the attached "Treatment" sheet so it does not read as a twin of page 3's "Treatment record". It holds the plan, treatments done, lab cases, LOAs and payment plans, so name it for that, for example "Plan, lab work and LOAs" (the owner may pick the word). Keep planned items OFF page 3: the Treatment record stays what was done and charged, the same on screen and paper (buildLedger, patient_balance()). The plan's consent gap, Mark done anyway with its reason, LOA waiting and Accept/Decline stay on the plan.

(c) Leave the health form's Save teal. It is hidden in its fold, and once the fold is open it is that form's only action. Make DeskConsent's Record consent quiet only together with an amber "No privacy consent on file" chip in the record's head, beside the safety chips, so the RA 10173 gap stays as visible as it is now. Otherwise leave it teal: it is not in the first screen, so the one-teal rule already holds.

(d) Dropped. The visit panel keeps its consent and signature cards, and the Treatment record keeps its consent and override rows (an owner ask in 035 and the owner's first pick in phase 4; "nothing hides that it went ahead").

(e) Remove the visually hidden h2s "Chart" and "Treatment record" inside the sheets. Point their regions' aria-labelledby at the visible sheet titles so each landmark keeps its name. Re-run paper-check (heading order, print, contrast at 1440 and 390, light and dark).
items.owner_question: Each box on the paper record that you can change has its own small plus: 53 on one patient. Would you rather have one quiet "Edit" per section instead, like a printed form? The boxes would still open with one tap.

items.title: Add patient (typed) shows 76 fields when only 2 are required, after two choosers
items.where: /c/<slug>/patients/new/ -> /patients/new/type/ (731 lines), src/lib/import.ts readPersonForm
items.problem: Typing in one patient takes 4 clicks over 2 screens to reach a 2726px form (5053px on a phone) with 76 visible fields, of which only last and first name are required. It mixes the person, HMO, 13 allergy ticks, 27 condition ticks, 6 medicine ticks, privacy consent, Past visits (an import concern: 'Most new patients have none') and an Opening balance (a migration concern). The page opens with its own three-way header repeating the chooser just answered.
items.proposal: Make the first screen: name, birth date, sex, mobile, allergies (with None known) and the privacy-consent choice, then Save. Fold address, emergency contact, HMO, conditions and medicines under 'More now' (or leave them to the record's medical history, which is where the paper form keeps them). Move Past visits and Opening balance to Import and to a 'Bring in old records' action on the record. Remove the type page's chooser header.
items.risk: Allergies and the minor/guardian rule must stay up front for patient safety. Clinics moving from paper use Past visits and Opening balance and must still find them (Import and the record). Edit details and import share readPersonForm, so flags such as has_paper_fields must keep older forms safe.
items.touches_owner_decision: Indirect only: 028 placed 'Patients fill it in' as Easiest beside typing. The typed form's contents were never an owner decision.
items.proposal_final:
Make "Type it in" (/c/<slug>/patients/new/type/) one short first screen without losing anything.

(a) Show what the desk always needs: last and first name, birth date with its age line, sex and mobile. Move middle name, suffix, email and HMO into the existing "Address, emergency contact and more" fold. That fold already opens by itself when a refused post comes back with something typed in it.

(b) Keep Health as one block with all three lists: allergies, conditions and medicines. Allergies stays open with None known. Conditions and medicines each become one line ("None" · "Add …"). The 27 condition and 6 medicine quick picks unfold only on "Add", so roughly 35 controls leave the first screen.
- A list nobody opened is still posted as unanswered (null), never as "None". readHealthForm already works this way.
- Ship this together with a fix to the Dashboard checklist (panels.ts fillCheck, from data.ts health_asked_at): when the latest version has any of the three lists null, the line must say what was not asked ("Health history: allergies asked <date>; conditions and medicines not asked"). It must not say "asked <date>".

(c) Leave the Privacy consent pane exactly as it is: DeskConsent with Not now, At the desk or Signed on paper, and the under-18 guardian rule (recordDeskConsent's minor check).

(d) Fold Past visits and Opening balance into one quiet line at the end: "Bringing in old records? Past visits and an opening balance". Keep the same single transaction, the same finance.bill gating and the same audit (appointment.import, invoice.import, payment.import). Moving them to a separate "Bring in old records" action on the record is optional and only if it sits under the record's More menu, since New booking stays the head's one teal. It would reuse insertVisits and insertMoney with openingKey's once-per-patient guard. Import already takes both.

(e) The three-way header on the type page:
- Keep the "forms sent / intakes not added yet" lines everywhere. They prevent duplicate patients.
- Hide the three ways only when the desk came through the chooser (index.astro adds a flag to its ./type/ link).
- When the chooser redirected straight here, which is every production request until the consent forms are reviewed, keep the 028 layout: Type it in, Patients fill it in (Easiest), Import a spreadsheet. It may be compacted to one line of two quiet links.

Correct the problem statement too: on production today, Add patient to the typed form is 2 clicks and 1 screen, not 4 clicks over 2 screens.

items.title: One glossary: the same things carry 2–4 names, and some names are simply stale
items.where: Site-wide: src/lib/messages.ts:134–144, src/pages/auth/forgot.astro:211, auth/login.astro:68, c/[clinic]/messages/index.astro:377, finances/*, patients/[patient].astro (contents), _record/*, account/, find/*
items.problem: Measured in rendered text and source. People vs Team: the section is People, but 7 user-facing strings (3 SMS texts to owners, the forgot page, a login error, Messages' 'Open Team to send a new code') say 'Settings -> Team' and link /settings/team/. Money: the button is 'New charge', the save is 'Save statement', the statement's lines are headed 'Charges', and numbers SOA-000001 and A-000001 sit in one list. Visits: workspace text says visit 44, booking 31 and appointment 9 times ('New booking', 'Appointments' sheet, 'My coming appointments', 'Next visit'). The patient side adds slot and request. Texts vs Messages: the page is 'Messages', the record sheet 'Texts', the action 'Text a patient'. Forms: 'New patient forms', 'Patient forms in progress', 'Forms sent', 'Open forms IN-…', 'consent forms'. The record: 'Treatment record' beside 'Treatment'.
items.proposal: Write a 1-page glossary in the repo and apply it in one sweep. Visit = the event; book = the verb (and 'request' only for a time the desk must place); statement = what a patient pays, with charge as a line on it; texts = SMS (rename the page 'Texts'); People; 'patient forms' = what a patient fills in, 'consent form' = a signed form; 'Treatment plan' for the attached sheet. Fix the 7 'Team' strings at once (S). Add a small check that fails the build on retired words in UI strings.
items.risk: SMS wording is GSM-safe and measured for length, so re-check segment counts. 'Invoice' must stay out of the UI because of the BIR line ('Flossify is not a BIR-registered invoicing system'). Printed statements and Rx are evidence, so change words on paper only with the owner's agreement.
items.touches_owner_decision: None standing. The BIR-related wording must be kept as is.
items.proposal_final:
One glossary: write a one-page glossary and apply it to the screens' own words only.

Step 1 (S, ship first). Change every leftover "Team" to People: forgot.astro:211, login.astro:68, messages/index.astro:259 and 377 (the link goes to /settings/#people; the /settings/team/ redirect stays), and both messages.ts prcMismatch texts ("Settings, People"). Keep them GSM-only, no arrow. Measure them again against 160 characters with a long dentist name and a seven-digit PRC number. If "Clinic settings, People" pushes them past one message, use "Settings, People".

Step 2 (M). Write the glossary:
- visit is the event, book is the verb, request is only a time the desk must place.
- statement is what a patient pays and charge is a line on it. The payment's paper stays "Acknowledgment of payment", never "receipt" or "invoice". SOA- and A- stay two separate numbered series.
- texts means SMS (Messages can become Texts; the URL stays or redirects).
- People.
- "patient forms" is what a patient fills in. Keep the QR- and IN- references that say where answers came from.
- "consent form" is a consent-library form in any state. Its state (to sign, signed, did not agree, withdrawn) is always shown beside it, and nothing unsigned may read as signed.
- The attached "Treatment" sheet is named for everything it holds (plan, work done, lab cases, LOAs, payment plans), not "Treatment plan". If no name fits, leave it and ask the owner.

Apply it in one sweep, with these left out:
(a) The consent library and TREATMENT_CONSENT, whose words are pinned by hash and versioned. They change only through a new version with a dentist's and the lawyer's review.
(b) /privacy/ (privacy-2026-09). It changes only as a new consent_version the lawyer has read.
(c) The paper record's printed labels copied from the owner's paper form, such as "Next visit" and "Patient information record".
(d) Printed and issued papers (statements, acknowledgments, Rx, letters, the A4 treatment record, aftercare sheets, which a dentist reads). They change only with the owner's agreement, and NOT_BIR stays verbatim.
(e) Identifiers: URLs (with redirects), audit event names, intents, message_log kinds, database values.

Patient texts keep every existing rule: GSM-only, no links, no request to reply, a named day; measure the length again.

The words check runs in tests rather than failing the build. It reads only on-screen UI strings and skips the files listed above.

items.title: Two signing mechanisms for the same consent, behind the same button label
items.where: /c/<slug>/patients/<id>/sign/<visit>/ (035 visit_consent, src/lib/visit-consent.ts), _record/ConsentRow.astro + intake start + /auth/park (039 consent_document), src/components/ws/cal/panels.ts:247, DeskConsent.astro, QR forms consent (patient_consent channel 'form')
items.problem: 'Sign on this tablet' in the calendar's visit panel opens the 035 tablet page: a clinic step, 'Hand the tablet to <name>', then strokes into visit_consent. 'Sign on this tablet' on the record's Consent row starts a 039 intake with the /auth/park hand-over, storing a consent_document. Both can sign the general consent (treatment-2026-09 is TREATMENT_CONSENT and also a library template). Privacy consent has 3 more paths: desk, paper, form. visit_treatment_consented() reconciles them, but a desk member learns two hand-over flows, and a maintainer keeps two signature pipelines, two print paths and two sets of tests.
items.proposal: Question for the owner and the lawyer: route every new signing through the 039 engine (one hand-over, one 'Thank you, hand it back' page, one sealed record), and keep 035's visit_consent rows readable and counted as now. Meanwhile (S), give the two buttons different words so the desk knows which one it is: 'Sign today's consent' (visit) and 'Sign this form'.
items.risk: Consent rows are legal evidence (RA 10173, the treatment consent). Nothing already signed may change, and the words in force must stay pinned (CONSENT_REVIEWED is empty, so production offers no 039 form yet). Moving the visit signing before review would leave production with no signing path, so the order matters.
items.touches_owner_decision: Consent records and the lawyer's review (CONSENT_REVIEWED, the review pack). The 035 tablet signing was the owner's ask ('the patient signs on an iPad'). This is a question, not a change.
items.proposal_final:
Title: One consent rule on screen now; one signing mechanism later, if the owner and the lawyer agree.

Now (S, no owner decision needed):
(a) One label for the 035 signing everywhere it appears: "Sign consent for this visit". That covers the calendar's Before we start (panels.ts:247), the Edit form's re-sign link (VisitPanel.astro:115), the record's This visit strip (VisitStrip.astro:108) and the visit panel (VisitPanels.astro:49, today "Sign consent on this tablet"). Do not say "today's": canSign allows future visits. Leave the 039 rows' "Sign on this tablet" / "Sign on their phone" as they are. They sit under the form's own title, and the tablet/phone choice is real.
(b) Make the This visit strip use the same rule as the calendar, visit_treatment_consented(). Today it reads only visit_consent (035), so a visit whose general consent was agreed through 039 says "signed" on the Dashboard and "not signed, Sign on this tablet" on the record. Nothing stored changes.

Question for the owner and the lawyer (L, after review):
"Once the dentist and your lawyer have read the general consent (treatment-2026-09), may every new signing — the visit's consent and the consent forms — go through the one hand-over (clinic tablet, this device, or their phone), with every consent already signed kept exactly as it is?"

Conditions if yes:
- Do it only after treatment-2026-09 is listed in CONSENT_REVIEWED. 035's page is not behind that gate and is today the only tablet signing on the live site, so moving earlier would leave production with none.
- Existing visit_consent rows stay readable and printable, and visit_treatment_consented() keeps counting them. Nothing is migrated or re-sealed.
- The 039 general consent must carry what 035's clinic step records: the plan lines the dentist explained, i.e. what "consentFor" shows. Otherwise the calendar's "signed for …" line and the Edit form's "have them sign again" prompt lose their basis.
