items.title: Settings and My page: one person's details on two pages, day-to-day choices buried in Clinic profile
items.where: /c/<slug>/settings/ (index 573 lines, settings.css 387), settings/people/[id].astro, /c/<slug>/account/
items.problem: Settings is one page of 2976px (4849 at 390) with 33 forms and 10 side panels. Its first section, Clinic profile, holds 9 groups: the public listing and contact details, but also 'How patients book online', 'Texts to patients' and the three 044 choices of 'How the day runs'. Those are operational, not profile, and an owner looking for reminders will not look under Profile. A person's details are split. My page shows username, email and mobile but says 'Change … on your page in Clinic settings'. The public-profile form exists on both pages. 'My days' is shown on My page but set in Settings. My page also has an Appearance block that duplicates the sidebar's theme switch (3 separate Save buttons on one page).
items.proposal: Move 'How patients book online', 'Texts to patients' and 'How the day runs' into an 'Appointments & reminders' section beside Opening hours and Closed days, and keep #work answering by redirecting the anchor. Make My page your own person page: the same component as settings/people/<id>, with the fields you may change editable, so there is one form per detail. Question for the owner: keep Appearance on My page or only in the sidebar.
items.risk: Rank rules (mayManage, BioValues, the ptr_seen guards) must hold on a merged component. Owners who learned the current place need the old anchors to keep working.
items.touches_owner_decision: The 044 choices were placed under Clinic profile -> How the day runs (not a standing rule). 'My page has Match my device · Light · Dark' is described in Art direction, so whether to remove it is a question.
items.proposal_final:
Title: Settings and My page: put the day-to-day choices in their own section, and make My page your own person page.

1) Appointments & reminders. Move "How patients book online" (booking_mode), "Texts to patients" (remind_48h, recall_texts) and "How the day runs" (turnover_min, hold_closed_reminders, consent_ask_at) out of Clinic profile. Put them in their own section, "Appointments & reminders", beside Opening hours and Closed days.
- The section gets its own form: a new `form=` value with a SECTION_OF entry, settings.edit only, <Csrf />.
- Its save does what the profile save does today, in one transaction: the same checks (the TURNOVERS list, booking_mode is live or request), holdClosedReminders() when hold_closed_reminders is turned on, and the 'clinic.settings' audit line.
- The profile save must keep what is saved for any of these six fields its form does not carry. Use a presence flag, as `has_work_choices` does now, so a profile save never refuses for a missing booking_mode and never switches reminders off.
- An older open tab that still posts the combined profile form keeps working: it carries the fields and is saved as today.
- Put `id="work"` on the new section's "How the day runs" heading, so `settings/#work` and choices-check.mjs keep landing without a script redirect.
- The listing line in Clinic profile that names the booking mode stays and reads the saved value.

2) My page as your own person page. Draw My page (/c/<slug>/account/) and settings/people/<id> from one shared component, so each detail has one form. What a person may change about themself stays exactly as it is now:
- Name, username, email, mobile, role and PRC number stay read only for the person. Only an owner or admin changes them, under mayManage (nobody changes their own role, an owner's row by an owner only). A new name or PRC number still goes back for the PRC check, and the one-email-one-mobile rule across the service still holds.
- Password stays on the self view only: the `?first=1#password` landing that requireWorkspace sends to while must_change_password is set, the throttle and auth_event lines, and the token_version bump.
- The PTR (action=ptr) is kept for signsPapers, with the ptr_seen/ptr_year_seen conflict guard and the 'staff.ptr' audit line.
- The public profile (action=bio, BioValues, 'staff.bio' audit) stays one form, shown once.
- My days stays read only for a person without people.manage.
- Verify the result as the 030/031 snapshots were verified: sign in as each of the seven roles, open My page and another person's page, and compare which fields are editable before and after.

3) Appearance stays on My page as it is. Its Match my device · Light · Dark is the only control that hands the theme back to the device (the sidebar switch only flips light/dark), so it is not a duplicate. It saves on tap and adds no Save button.

Question for the owner: none needed. Both moves only change where things are, and the owner's words ("each clinic's own choice", "light or dark is the person's choice") still hold.

items.title: CLAUDE.md is a 159KB history book; the next maintainer needs a 300-line rulebook
items.where: CLAUDE.md (1886 lines), docs/HANDOFF.md, docs/workspace-redesign.md (827 lines)
items.problem: CLAUDE.md is 24,212 words (about 40k tokens) loaded into every session. 62 of its lines describe reversed, retired or historical states, including a 57-line block on the superseded twelve-part record and the 27 Sep colour-coding and pill rounds. Headings are stale ('The schedule — /c/<slug>/schedule/' names a redirect; 'Treatment record — page 4 … the record's second section' contradicts 'Page 3: Treatment record'). 3 references point to tools that lived only in a past session's scratchpad (entrance-check.mjs, snap.mjs/cmp.mjs, intake-spec.md). The handoff it sends readers to first says 1 Oct and 'migrations through 043', while main has 045 and 35 later commits.
items.proposal: Split it. CLAUDE.md keeps standing constraints, art direction, verification, traps and the invariants that protect patients and money (RLS, CSRF, consent, the balance, texts with no links), aiming for 300 lines or fewer. Each feature's design and history moves to docs/features/<area>.md, linked from a short index. Reversed history is deleted (git keeps it). HANDOFF.md is updated or folded into a 'Where things stand' section. The scratchpad tools are committed under scripts/dev/ or their references removed.
items.risk: The 'why' behind owner decisions must not be lost: quote the standing decisions verbatim and keep a link to the history. Agents that rely on details now in feature docs must be told where to look (the index).
items.touches_owner_decision: None. The standing constraints are carried over word for word.
items.proposal_final:
Split CLAUDE.md into a rulebook of 300 to 400 lines plus feature documents.

**CLAUDE.md keeps:**
- Standing constraints, art direction, The tour's motion and footer rules, Verification and Traps, carried over word for word with the owner's quotes.
- A new short section, "Patient data you must not handle", lifted from the record's history:
  - Never open another clinic's admin or patient pages behind its login. Ask the owner to describe them, or to send screenshots with the patient's details covered.
  - Never save or share photos or screenshots that show a real patient's details. Use them for layout only.
- A short "Retired — do not bring back" list, one line each with the owner's quote and the date:
  - the Swiss rules
  - the Three.js scene
  - the film limited to the opening section
  - the footer and the readout rail
  - the Reduce Motion gating
  - the twelve-part record
  - the record's colour coding by group (27 Sep)
  - the tooth chart on the home page
- The invariants that protect patients, consent and money:
  - RLS and `withClinic`, and the app never connecting as a superuser
  - CSRF and rate limits
  - Settings read from `process.env` only
  - Consent words versioned and pinned (`body_sha256`, `CONSENT_REVIEWED`, new words mean a new version and a new row)
  - The privacy notice's words changed together with `retention_purge()`, and the version hard-coded in `/privacy/`
  - `FORMS_PRIVACY_VERSIONS` keeping the patient forms closed until a notice covers them
  - The insert-only tables: `clinical_note`, `visit_consent`, `consent_*`, `vital_sign`, `day_close` and `appointment_contact`
  - Sign-in codes never rendered on any page
  - No links in a text, and no text asking for a reply
  - `patient_balance()` as the one balance
  - BIR invoices coming from the clinic's own booklet
  - `BILLING_FINAL` staying false until the owner sets real prices
  - PRC licences checked by a person
  - Allergy and alert visibility on the record and the Dashboard
  - Offline charting's rules
  - Migrations as new numbered files only
- The whole "Open — read before shipping" list, kept up to date.
- A "Where things stand" section that replaces HANDOFF.md, or a HANDOFF.md updated to match main (migrations to 045).
- An index of the feature documents.

**docs/features/<area>.md** gets each feature's design, measurements and the reasons behind it. Move the text and do not rewrite it, so no owner quote is lost. Reversed history may be deleted (git keeps it), but only after its "do not bring back" line exists in CLAUDE.md.

**The scratchpad tools** (entrance-check.mjs, snap.mjs and cmp.mjs, intake-spec.md) are committed under scripts/dev/ or docs/. If they cannot be recovered, their references are removed and the method is described in a sentence.

**Check before merging:**
- Grep the old file for every quote in italics or straight quotes, every "never", "do not" and "must" sentence, and every table, function or setting name.
- Confirm each one appears in the new CLAUDE.md or in a feature document linked from the index.
- Ask the owner to read the new Standing constraints and the "Retired" list.

items.title: Two parallel component systems drawn identically, and shared classes redefined in up to 21 files
items.where: src/styles/global.css (.btn* vs .ws-btn*, .card vs .ws-pane, the '.ws .btn' layer), every page CSS; class families pill/chip/tag/callout/head
items.problem: The site's .btn/.btn-primary/.btn-quiet (389/114/243 uses) and the workspace's .ws-btn/.ws-btn-primary/.ws-btn-quiet (345/100/230) are the same button, with a '.ws .btn*' override layer to keep them equal. .ws-btn-sm is 44px tall like the normal one. Pills and tags come in 7+ classes (ws-pill 61, rp 79, rk 15, chip 45, ik-tag 7, tag 15, ws-chip 3). Callouts come as ws-callout (103) plus four page-local kinds, and there are 28 different '*-head' classes. Confirmations come in 3 styles (native confirm() x3, a side panel, a ?confirm= page). Shared classes are re-declared elsewhere: .ws-icon in 21 places, .ws-btn 10, .meta 10, .field 10, .ws-callout 8. The 'pt-' prefix means the public patient pages in patient.css and Today's patients in cal.css, with pt-main, pt-name, pt-sub and pt-side defined in both.
items.proposal: Pick one name per pattern (button, card, pill with tones, callout, panel, plus, page head). Alias the other for one release, then sweep. Forbid re-declaring a shared class outside global.css except through a modifier class. Keep a short prefix registry in global.css's header so prefixes never collide. Replace native confirm() with the side-panel confirm.
items.risk: Visual regressions in the workspace. Use the Site API rule (compare computed styles before and after) and the existing contrast checks; nothing should look different.
items.touches_owner_decision: None. The soft template's look is unchanged; only names merge.
items.proposal_final:
Title: one name per pattern, with the paper and glass scopes kept, and the offline guards left alone.

1. **Merge the names, not the looks.** Pick one name each for button, card/pane, pill with tones, callout, panel, plus and page head. Alias the old names for one release, then sweep them out. Start with the biggest wins:
   - `.btn*` and `.ws-btn*`, removing the `.ws .btn*` override layer
   - the pill and tag family: `ws-pill`, `rp`, `rk`, `chip`, `ik-tag`, `tag`, `ws-chip`, as one pill with tones
   - `ws-callout` and the page-local callouts
   - `.ws-btn-sm`, which is the same 44 px as the normal button: drop it or make it the same class
   - the `pt-` collision: rename Today's patients' classes in cal.css, because `pt-` is the public patient pages' prefix

   Keep every status pill as words plus colour, never colour alone. The QUEUE classes stay the only status colours.

2. **One home for shared classes, with named scopes.** A shared class is defined only in global.css, inside `@layer components`. Elsewhere it may change only through a modifier class or one of these registered scopes:
   - `.pp-sheet`: the paper record, record.css "The record on paper"
   - the glass scopes: `.pt-glass`, `.cl-glass`, `.wb-glass`, `.me-shell`, `cv-*`, `.pane-glass`
   - `.entrance` and its `--en-*`
   - print pages
   - `public/samples/` (outside the system)

   List the scopes and the prefix registry in global.css's header. When a class is renamed, move its scoped rules in the same change. On the sheet a pill still reads as plain words, and an allergy (`rp-alert`) and a warning (`rp-warn`) keep their red and amber emphasis.

   Collapse plain duplicates that do not change the look: the 21 copies of `.ws-icon`, and the re-declared `.ws-btn`, `.meta`, `.field` and `.ws-callout`.

3. **Confirmations: one pattern, without weakening any question.**
   - Change: the record's `data-confirm` forms (LOA not approved on Mark done, Take off plan, Remove file, Stop plan, Cancel LOA) may move to the side-panel confirm, with the same sentences. Draw the panel from the server so it also works with scripts off, as the patient forms' `?confirm=` page does. Keep that page as the scripts-off path.
   - Leave as they are: the sign-out guard in `offline-queue.ts` (it warns about unconfirmed chart changes and must work offline and synchronously) and Odontogram's "Delete … never saved" confirm. Move either only if the offline checks prove a side panel blocks sign-out and deletion just as reliably, offline and on every page with a sign-out.

4. **Verify by measurement:**
   - Compare computed styles before and after on the workspace, the public pages, the glass pages, the paper sheet (both themes), and print.
   - Run `paper-check.mjs`, `dash-check.mjs`, `phone-e2e.mjs` and the glass contrast measures at 1440 and 390, light and dark. Nothing may look or measure different.
   - Run a Tailwind build-CSS diff, since class names are scanned.

Owner decision touched: none. The paper record, the glass and the soft look are unchanged, only names merge.

items.title: CSS that only undoes CSS: the record's reversed layers, dead classes and 600 local colours
items.where: src/pages/c/[clinic]/patients/_record/record.css (1070 lines, 84KB), src/styles/global.css, all CSS
items.problem: The record's parts are still rendered as glass panes, pills (.rp, .rk) and tiles from the 27 Sep 'every detail its own pill' and colour-coding rounds, then flattened on the paper by 113 '.pp-sheet' rules, 35 of which only reset border, background, padding or display. The .hue-* colour system reversed on 2 Oct is still defined and used in 10 places, and record.css has 8 !important. Across the site, 1933 classes are defined, 70 used nowhere (e.g. pp-facts, pp-lines, tl-*, rf-*, on-invert, grid-frame, theme-switch-*) and 1396 (72%) in a single file. 600 raw hex colours live outside global.css's tokens (record.css 124). Each of the 39 dark rules needs its twin in 25 files.
items.proposal: Render the record's sections as paper markup directly (no ws-pane or rp inside .pp-sheet), then delete the flatten-and-reset rules and the hue and pill layers. Delete the 70 unused classes. Move local colours to tokens (paper ink, pen ink and band are already tokens). Generate the dark twins from one mixin or token block so a rule cannot miss one.
items.risk: The paper look and its measured contrast (lowest 4.68:1) could drift, so re-run paper-check light and dark at 1440 and 390. Components such as DeskConsent are shared with the rest of the workspace, so their workspace look must not change.
items.touches_owner_decision: The record on paper (4 Oct) stays exactly as it looks today; this only changes how it is built.
items.proposal_final:
CSS that only undoes CSS. Remove the record's reversed layers without changing anything a person sees.

1. **Render the paper directly.** On the three sheets and the attached sheets, the record's parts render paper markup directly, with no `ws-pane` tiles or pill chrome inside `.pp-sheet`. Then delete the reset-only `.pp-sheet` rules. Keep the paper's own emphasis as paper classes: an allergy or alert in red (today `.rp-alert`) and a warning in amber (today `.rp-warn`). The warnings include "Newer words: sign again", "Addendum", "Went ahead anyway", withdrawals, "Did not agree" and money owed. Every consent state, signature slip and override line keeps its words. Shared components (DeskConsent, ConsentRow, Notes, VisitPanels) keep their workspace look outside the sheet.

2. **Hue and pills outside the sheet.** Keep `.rp`, `.rk` and the hue tokens where the workspace still draws them: the visit panel and the This visit strip. Retiring the visit panel's per-section colours (`hue-teal`, `hue-violet`, `hue-blue`, `hue-rose`, `hue-green`) fits the 2 Oct reversal of colour groups, but it changes what people see. List it to the owner as a visible change, not as a refactor.

3. **Unused classes.** Delete a class only after it has been checked against:
   - classes built at runtime (template literals, `class:list`, `classList`, data-driven `TONE` maps), e.g. `theme-switch-${variant}`
   - the DOM rendered across every page type in both themes
   - scripts/ (audit.mjs reads `.on-invert`)
   - print media

   Keep the theme switch's focus rings.

4. **Raw colours to tokens.** Move raw colours to tokens on screen styles only. Leave these exceptions with their own fixed colours, or give them one fixed paper palette that never changes with the theme:
   - the SwiftCare sample (its own token block; it must not import global.css)
   - every print page (black on white whatever the theme): statements with their BIR wording, Rx and letters with PRC/PTR, consent and forms printouts, aftercare, the treatment-record paper
   - the record's `@media print` rules and their `!important`

   Any colour change on glass pages (`_Door`, `_Shell`, `clinic-glass.css`) is measured again against the pixels behind it.

5. **Dark twins from one source.** For example, tokens defined once with `light-dark()` and `color-scheme` set from `data-theme`, or one token block per theme. It must still honour both the device's preference and the person's choice: chosen dark = device dark, chosen light = device light. The paper sheet stays light in both themes, while panels and popovers opened inside it follow the person's theme.

**Verify:**
- paper-check (light and dark, 1440 and 390, lowest ≥ 4.68:1)
- the printed record (page 1 still one A4 sheet) and the treatment-record and statement printouts
- seat-check and dash-check for the visit panel
- a snapshot of computed styles on workspace pages before and after: the workspace must not change except where the owner approved it in point 2

items.title: Eight print pages, eight stylesheets, and the Treatment record printed two ways
items.where: finances/[invoice]/print.astro, patients/[patient]/{rx,letters,aftercare,consents/[document]/print,treatment-record}.astro, patients/forms/[form]/print.astro, patients/qr/print.astro, record.css print block
items.problem: 8 print pages are documents of their own, each with its own inline stylesheet of 37–63 lines (402 lines in all; 6 as a pageCss template literal) and 29–50 hex colours each, plus the record's own print block. The Treatment record prints from 'Print the record' (pages 1–3) and again from its own Print button (/treatment-record/), so there are two layouts of one ledger to keep identical.
items.proposal: One PaperPage layout with one paper.css (A4/A5, the clinic's letterhead from Letterhead.astro, black on white, page feet) used by every print. Print the Treatment record from the record's print with a 'this page only' choice, and keep /treatment-record/ as a redirect.

items.proposal_final:
Title: One paper shell for the seven print pages; the Treatment record drawn one way.

**What is shared**
- **A PaperPage layout** handles what every print page repeats today: the screen bar (the way back and one teal Print, never printed), ParkedGuard, the black-on-white print tokens for both themes, and the paper size as a prop. The sizes are A4, A5 and the statement's 80 mm receipt with its script-measured length.
- **One paper.css** holds the shared pieces: the bar, the sheet, small print, sign-off lines, feet and table rules. It replaces the repeated `.px-*` / `.pr-*` / `.fp-*` blocks and their hex colours.
- **A PaperHead component** takes a clinic face as a prop: name, address, phone, email, plus the TIN and branch code on statements.
  - Statements, prescriptions, letters, aftercare sheets, the patient-forms printout and the Treatment record pass the clinic's current row, as they do now.
  - The consent print passes the signing's stored snapshot (`clinicFace` / `snapshotDoc`), never the current row.
  - Do not reuse Letterhead.astro: its Chart #, opened date and Edit button belong to page 1 of the record only.

**What each paper keeps**
- Its own body, wording and checks, unchanged:
  - Statements: NOT_BIR, the TIN, and the BIR receipt number or a blank to write it in.
  - Prescriptions and letters: the prescriber's PRC (read live) and the PTR copy taken when the paper was saved (041).
  - Consents: the "Unchanged since it was stored" check or its red line, the "CF-… · version" and "Page x of y" feet, and the ?paper=1 gate.
- Its own audit action: invoice.print / payment.print, record.rx_print, record.letter_print, record.aftercare_print, consent.print, forms.print.

**What is left out**
- The QR poster (patients/qr/print.astro and _poster.ts). It is a millimetre drawing that must still scan.

**The Treatment record**
- Make /treatment-record/ draw the same TreatmentRecord component and print rules the record uses for page 3, inside PaperPage. The ledger then has one layout.
- Keep it a server-rendered page, not a redirect, so `record.treatment_record_print` is still written by the server when it opens.
- Add NOT_BIR (when finance.bill shows amounts), SIGN_LEGEND and "Printed <date> by <name>" to that shared page-3 print. The record's own "Print the record" then carries the BIR line too; today it does not.
- Optionally, the record's print can offer "Treatment record only", which opens that page.

**Check before and after**
- Snapshot each paper's printed text (PRC and PTR lines, NOT_BIR, TIN, consent check line and feet, page feet).
- Check for overflow at A4, A5 and 80 mm, with money and without (finance.bill).
- Confirm the consent print shows the snapshot's clinic even after the clinic's address has changed in Settings.

items.title: A clinic's public page lives at two addresses, each canonical to itself
items.where: src/pages/[clinic]/index.astro and src/pages/find/[clinic]/index.astro (both render find/_ui/ClinicPage.astro), find/[clinic]/book.astro, src/layouts/Base.astro canonical
items.problem: /find/<slug>/ (linked from Find a clinic, the home page's Partners and dentist pages) and /<slug>/ ('the clinic's own site', linked only from Settings) draw the same body: 1475 and 1421px, 16/20 controls, 2 teal each. Base.astro makes each canonical to itself, so search engines see duplicate pages, and an owner sharing the link has two to choose from. Each also shows two teal 'Book a slot' buttons.
items.proposal: Question for the owner: make /<slug>/ the one address (the one a clinic prints and shares), with /find/<slug>/ redirecting or carrying a canonical to it, or the reverse. Keep booking at one address too. Make the header's Book the quiet twin on both.
items.risk: Links already shared, and the 'All clinics' back link from /find/ context, which needs a referrer-aware back link.
items.touches_owner_decision: Clinic doors and the clinic's own site (029 P5), where the owner chose /<slug>/ as the clinic's site. Which address wins is a question.
items.proposal_final:
Title: Settings shows one address for a clinic's public page, and search engines see one page

Where:
- src/layouts/Base.astro: add an optional `canonical` prop, used for <link rel=canonical>, og:url and the JSON-LD url.
- src/pages/find/[clinic]/index.astro: pass that prop.
- src/pages/c/[clinic]/settings/_ui/ProfileSection.astro: the two address blocks.
- Optional: src/pages/find/[clinic]/book.astro, its back link.

Problem: /find/<slug>/ and /<slug>/ draw the same body (find/_ui/ClinicPage.astro), and each names itself as canonical. Search engines see two copies of every clinic's page. Settings → Clinic profile offers the owner both addresses, one under the other: "See your public page" goes to /find/<slug>/, and "Your clinic's own page: flossify.ph/<slug>" sits under it. The owner has to guess which one to print and share.

Proposal (no visible page changes, keeps both pages):
1. Keep both pages, with no redirect.
   - /<slug>/ is the clinic's own site (P5, the owner's request): its own bar and Staff sign-in.
   - /find/<slug>/ is the same clinic inside Find a clinic: the patients' bar, "All clinics" and "Other clinics".
2. Point /find/<slug>/'s canonical and og:url at https://flossify.ph/<slug>/, the address the owner already calls "your clinic's own page".
   - Exception: a clinic whose slug is in RESERVED (src/lib/slug.ts) has no /<slug>/ page, so its canonical stays /find/<slug>/.
3. In Settings, show one address. Merge the two blocks into one line: "Your clinic's page: flossify.ph/<slug> (Open, Copy)", with the team's sign-in address under it as now. "See your public page" then opens /<slug>/ (or /find/<slug>/ for a reserved slug).
4. Optional, small: carry ?from=site on the Book links drawn on /<slug>/. The booking's back link then returns to /<slug>/ instead of the Find a clinic version.

Not part of this (already true, so it was dropped from the original):
- The header's Book is already quiet on both pages.
- Booking is already one address, /find/<slug>/book/.
- The page's two teal Book buttons are at its head and its end, never in the same screen.

Effort: S. Impact: 2.

Verify: fetch both URLs and read back the canonical. Fetch a reserved-slug clinic if the database has one. Open Settings at 1440 and 390: one address line, contrast at least 4.5:1, targets at least 44 px.

dropped.title: A phone downloads the whole 4MB film before the visitor scrolls
dropped.why:
ask-owner: The facts check out. In src/pages/index.astro, lines 653-657 set `vid.src` and call `vid.load()` as soon as the script runs, and the video tag has `preload="auto"`. tour-960.mp4 is 3,973,540 bytes and tour-1440.mp4 is 9,265,533 bytes. docs/generation.md:160 says the poster is frame 0. The change removes no legal, clinical or data duty: the film carries no consent, privacy, audit, PRC, BIR or safety content.

It does touch a decision the owner made twice. CLAUDE.md, The tour, says the owner first objected to "a version that gave the film no `src` under Reduce Motion (they saw stills)", and then wrote "THE CINEMATIC MOTION SHOULD ALWAYS BE ON, ITS NOT AN OPTION". Loading on first interaction gates nothing and the walk still runs for every visitor. But it brings back, briefly, the very thing the owner complained about: an opening still with no film behind it. On a slow line the first scroll would hold on the poster until the data arrives. A quiet change could be read as watering that decision down, so it has to go to the owner as a question, which the auditor also suggested.

One correction to the proposal. The `requestIdleCallback`-after-first-paint option fires within milliseconds of paint, so it still downloads the whole 4 MB before a patient can tap "I'm a Patient". It saves nothing and should be dropped. Only a load that waits for the visitor to interact delivers the saving. | drop: This is a performance change, not a simplification, and the measurements show the problem is much smaller than claimed for the person it names.

1. **The code matches the claim.** In `src/pages/index.astro` (lines 652-657), the script sets `vid.src` to `tour-960.mp4` on screens 900px wide or less (`tour-1440.mp4` otherwise) and calls `vid.load()` right after layout. The video tag has `preload="auto"`. The phone file is 3,973,540 bytes and the desk file 9,265,533 bytes. Both have the index (moov) at the front, and the dev server answers byte ranges with 206. `docs/generation.md` confirms the poster is frame 0, so the first screen looks the same either way.

2. **The auditor's measurement can't be right as stated.** Headless Chromium has no H.264. With the real MP4 it fires `error` after about 391KB, so it never "fetched tour-960.mp4 in full". The 3.97MB is just the file's Content-Length.

3. **What I measured instead.** I routed the film to a VP9 copy of about the same size (4.9MB) through a server that supports byte ranges, and counted bytes in the browser through CDP.
   - **Wi-Fi, 390px, 12s, no scroll:** Chromium pulled the whole file. So the claim holds on Wi-Fi, but there the data costs nothing.
   - **Same, with the connection type set to cellular4g or cellular3g:** Chromium itself reports `vid.preload === "metadata"`. It forces metadata on mobile connections and stopped at 1.1–1.6MB of the 4.9MB copy. Scaled to the real file, that is roughly 1MB, not 4MB.
   - **Throttled to 4 Mbps down, 100 ms latency:** in the first 6s about 0.7–0.8MB arrived whether preload was auto or metadata. Leaving the page stops the download, so a patient who taps I'm a Patient at once never pays 4MB.
   - I did not measure iOS Safari, which also holds back preload on phones. Android Chrome, the main browser in the Philippines, behaves like the cellular runs above.

4. **The trade-off.** I simulated the proposal on the same 4 Mbps profile by holding the film request until the first scroll. The first moving frame came 80–190 ms later than now (1130 vs 1317 ms when scrolling during the load, 625 vs 707 ms when scrolling at 4s). The poster's arrival was the same in both cases (about 2.43s), so the first paint gains nothing.

5. **It simplifies nothing.** The patient and the clinic owner see the same screen with the same steps and words. The change adds code (an interaction listener and an idle callback) to the one script the owner is most sensitive about. The owner once saw stills where the film had no src, and "motion always on" is a standing rule. The effort estimate (S) is fair, but impact 2 is overstated. The real saving is at most about 1MB on mobile data, and only for someone who leaves without scrolling.

**Keep out of the simplification plan.** If a separate performance list is ever kept, this could go there as a low-priority note, measured on a real Android phone on mobile data first. It should not go to the owner as a simplification question.

The temporary script `scripts/dev/.plan-marketing-film.tmp.mjs` and the scratch videos are deleted.

dropped.title: Open the grid on who is still in the clinic, not on the clock
dropped.why:
keep: This doesn't reverse any owner decision or remove any obligation. Where the grid opens on load is set by `scrollToStart()` in src/components/ws/cal/board.ts (today: now minus 60 min; other days: the first visit minus 30, else opening time). That rule came in with the 26 Sep workspace redesign as a design default. Nothing in CLAUDE.md, docs/workspace-redesign.md or the git history quotes the owner asking for the grid to open on the clock. The proposal also fits the owner's 3 Oct brief for a dentist who runs the clinic ("ease of access and better user experience"; "the first screen gives way to the day"), because the people actually in the clinic come into view.

It removes nothing that has to be kept:
- No consent, audit, privacy, PRC or BIR wording is involved.
- The cards still show the same allergy and alert information. Bringing the in-chair and waiting patients into view, with their "Waiting N min" amber words, makes safety and waiting cues easier to see, not harder.
- The phone list is untouched (`scrollToStart` returns early on a phone).
- Week view and other days keep their current rule.
- The live 30 s refresh does not re-scroll, because only `S.scrollTo` triggers a scroll, so nothing moves under the person.

Points for whoever builds it:
- Pick the anchor from `shownTimed()`, so a dentist's Mine view anchors on their own patients.
- Leave out done, cancelled and no-show visits.
- Keep the proposed cap of about 3 hours before now, so an unclosed early visit or a forgotten no-show cannot pin the grid all day.
- Re-check dash-check.mjs's first-screen measurements afterwards (the grid starts at 613 px at 1440 × 900). | drop: I re-measured on :4610 as liwayway at session-road, with the browser clock fixed. The mechanism is real, but the problem is much smaller than claimed, and the change isn't a simplification.

What the code does: `scrollToStart()` in src/components/ws/cal/board.ts scrolls today's grid to "now − 60 min" at 2.2 px a minute, and it does nothing on phones. At 11:35 the grid opened at scrollTop 209 in a 465 px frame (413 px at 1366). The 9:00–9:45 in-chair card and the 9:30–10:15 in-lobby card had 0 px in view, and only the 10:15 card showed. So far the auditor is right.

**1. The scenario comes from the seed data.** The seed puts visits at fixed times (9:00 in chair, 9:30 in lobby, 10:15 confirmed) with "live" statuses, whatever the hour of the test. At 9:50 all three cards are fully in view (scrollTop 0). For an unfinished visit to be off the grid, its booked end has to be more than an hour in the past. That means a 45-minute filling still in the chair 1h50 later, or a patient waiting two hours. In a real clinic that is almost always someone who forgot to press Done, not a person still in the room.

**2. The desk isn't looking at an empty grid.** At both 1440×900 and 1366×768, the first screen already shows these two people three times:
- the tiles: "Waiting 1 · here, not seated yet" and "In the chair 1"
- Next for you, at y=253: "In your chair 9:00 am Maria Liza Dela Cruz … Done"
- Today's patients, with each row's one-tap next step (Maria in the first screen at both sizes, Anna at 1440)

The grid barely reaches the first screen anyway. Its frame starts at 613 px at 1440, so 230 px of the grid is visible. At 1366×768 the frame starts at 665, leaving 46 px. To use the grid at all you scroll the page first.

**3. It costs something, and adds nothing simpler.** Today there is one rule anyone can predict: the grid opens an hour before now. The proposal makes the opening point depend on statuses, so it moves from day to day. It also uses up the afternoon: the 1366 frame shows only about 162 minutes, so anchoring 2–3 hours back pushes the now line and the afternoon out of view. The afternoon is what the desk needs to book a phone caller.

Including "late" visits would anchor on no-shows all day; those belong on Calls. The proposal as worded also reads every visit at the clinic, not just the ones shown. For Hazel (Mine, an empty column) at 10:50 it would scroll up an empty column. And a forgotten status should be fixed by pressing Done, which the first screen already offers.

The effort really is small (a few lines in `scrollToStart`). But the value is low, it's polish rather than simplification, and it trades a predictable view for an unpredictable one, so I'd leave it out of the plan.

If someone does want it later, the safe version would:
- count only arrived, in lobby and in chair, and only among the visits shown
- reach back no further than keeps the now line in the frame (target ≥ now − visible minutes + 30)
- be rated impact 1, not 3

I deleted the measuring script (scripts/dev/.plan-dashboard-scroll.tmp.mjs) and changed nothing else.
